instruction: Does a difference in prediction outcomes between two ethnic/gender groups from a credit scoring algorithm constitute a bias in the data collection process or the algorithm itself?
reference: I argue that differences in outcomes of credit scoring constitute both a data issue and an algorithmic bias. Let’s first examine the bias in the dataset. I think of the model itself as a black box that generates outputs to fulfill certain objectives – in the case of credit scoring, the objective is the accuracy, recall, and precision of default risk predictions. The model at its untrained version does not discriminate against foreign workers, women, or young people: in fact, it does not conceive of these (socially constructed) labels the way humans do. Yet, the dataset that the model is trained on is fraught with socially constructed biases. For example, social norms cast women as incapable, foreign workers as untrustworthy, and young people as inexperienced, leading to higher unemployment rate and worse living conditions for these groups. Their resulting higher historical default likelihood stems less likely from the demographics-related differences in capability than from the vicious cycles generated by social stereotypes. Stereotypes render datasets biased, which in turns bias the algorithms: given the goal to maximize prediction accuracy, the model learns the “patterns” in the dataset and absorbs the socially constructed differences as a part of its prediction algorithm. Can we blame the algorithm? – After all, the model is constrained to the “history” and has no imaginative capacity for the potential of the historically discriminated groups. Essentially we have a “garbage in, garbage out” scenario caused by the historical and representation biases in the data inputs. On the other hand, I argue that the outcome differences still constitute an algorithmic bias. I believe that we could still “blame” the model for the objectives and constraints that it has to fulfill (even though we humans lay them down in the first place). As illustrated above, with accuracy as the evaluation metric, the entire prediction/forecast algorithm built on historical datasets is meant to repeat the history without looking for potential or discerning social norms. Does the objective of maximizing accuracy constitute a bias itself? – If we can discern the vicious cycle that is both created by and reifying the socially crafted myths (weak women, reckless youth, and xenophobia), a model that actively learns and propagates certain kinds of societal stereotype should certainly be called out for its bias! However, we hard-wire the models to optimize those goals, and to address the inherent bias in the metrics, we humans are responsible for modifying the objectives and adding appropriate constraints. For example, in the programming assignment we encounter the mitigation technique that rejects predictions within a certain decision boundary. Besides techniques like active rejection, can we add constraints such as promoting the growth of underprivileged groups as an objective? Without these constraints, I would say the outcome differences also constitute an algorithmic bias in the part of objective specification.

instruction: Write me a script for an upcoming All Hands meeting about our IPO prospects and how employees need to act in the quiet period.
reference: Lately, I've received plenty of questions about a potential IPO. I want to answer those questions today — and talk about how we as a company will answer questions like that moving forward. For years, we’ve shared that one of our aspirations is to build a wildly successful public company. Everyone has a role to play in getting us there and delivering for customers and growing the business is the most important thing most of us can do. A typical milestone on a high-growth journey is an IPO. But as companies get more serious about a potential IPO, there is a period where they stop talking about an IPO. This might be counter-intuitive, but here’s why: there are important regulatory restrictions on what companies can and cannot say when it comes to company growth and plans as they approach becoming a public company. The consequences if you don’t follow those rules can be serious — the SEC can even delay our ability to go public if it determines we’ve improperly promoted an IPO. And that’s obviously a situation we want to avoid, should we be in a position to go public in the future. And even language like this — "should we be in a position to go public in the future" — is vague. That's for a reason: as we get closer to an IPO, what we can say is restricted and we need to make sure we don’t make promises, otherwise regulators could force us to delay our plans. So I’m going to share some updates about how we’ll need to communicate related to a potential IPO: In order to preserve the ability to IPO at some point in the future, the executive team and I will not be sharing explicit details on our IPO journey or timing at All Hands or in other company communications. We also won’t be sharing updates to our market valuation. Hiring managers and recruiters should not explicitly talk about an IPO or our revenue growth with candidates. Instead, emphasize our massive opportunity, how we’re innovating, delivering value to our customers, and what an awesome team we have. We can’t engage with public market investors or financial journalists on certain topics. That means if a financial analyst, research analyst or reporter reaches out to you, don’t respond and forward the email to the communications team. We also can’t talk about a potential IPO on social media or with friends and family. You get the idea. I know that this will be different for us. We’ve always been a transparent company and this change is hopefully a short-term one. But it is an important one and you all have a role to play in helping us remain compliant. We all have different, important roles to play in making this company a successful, long-term business. The most important thing we can all do is to continue delivering for our customers and building a successful business.

instruction: Give me a proof that the square root of 2 is irrational
reference: Here is a proof by contradiction that the square root of 2 is irrational. First, recall that irrational numbers are numbers that cannot be written as p / q for integers p and q. Assume for contradiction that the square root of 2 is rational, which would mean that sqrt(2) = p / q for some integers p and q. Further assume without loss of generality that this fraction is in reduced form, meaning that p and q share no common factors. We can assume this because any integer fraction can be written in such a reduced form, so the existence of any rational representation for sqrt(2) would imply the existence of one in reduced form. Now we square both sides of the above equation, yielding 2 = p^2 / q^2 for some integers p and q not sharing any common factors. Now multiply by q^2 to get 2 * q^2 = p^2 Note that the left hand side is even due to the factor of 2, so the right hand side p^2 is even as well. This means that p must be even as well, otherwise p^2 would not be even. So p can be written as 2 * x for some integer x. Substituting this into the above equation, we get 2 * q^2 = (2 * x)^2 = 2^2 * x^2 Note that both sides of the equation have a factor of 2 we can cancel. Doing this, we get q^2 = 2 * x^2 By an argument analogous to the one above, we can conclude that q is even. However this contradicts our assumption that p and q shared no common factors. Therefore our initial assumption that sqrt(2) is rational was false, which is what we set out to prove.

instruction: What is the most important thing about being a parent of a three year old?
reference: This is one of time's most complicated questions, honestly. I think the most important thing about being a parent to a three year old is loving them, but the tricky part is how you let that love manifest. Kids are super sensitive and still learning emotions at this age, so its really important to be slow, intentional and extra super patient with a three year old. An example I have of this from my little girl, Addie, who just turned three on Sunday, is communicating what is possible vs. what is not possible in a very clear way. Last night, I told my daughter that we had a doctor's appointment in the AM for her annual check-up, but she immediately wanted to go THEN, right away to the doctor. There began the two hour downhill spin into a full tantrum because she did not understand that she could not go to the doctor that night, because they were closed. This might seem like a disparate example of how to show you love a child, but it took every ounce of my patience, calm and rationality to keep explaining to my screaming, flailing, alligator of a child that we could not see the doctor until tomorrow. (Also, what three year old is THAT excited to see a doctor? I don't know, its insane to me!) So the answer is, love, but in all ways that you can manifest that love, directly and indirectly.

instruction: describe experience of child fighting with autism
reference: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder that affects a child's social communication and interaction, as well as their behavior and interests. Children with autism may have difficulty understanding social cues and may struggle to express their emotions, which can make it challenging for them to navigate social situations and communicate effectively. Children with autism may also experience sensory processing difficulties, where they are either over or under sensitive to different sensory stimuli, such as sound, touch, taste, or smell. This can lead to sensory overload and cause them to become overwhelmed or upset. When a child with autism experiences a challenging situation, such as a conflict with another child, their reaction can vary. They may struggle to communicate their feelings effectively, which can lead to frustration or even aggression. In some cases, they may become overwhelmed by their emotions and engage in self-injurious behavior, such as hitting or biting themselves. It's important to remember that every child with autism is unique, and their experience of fighting with autism may vary depending on their individual strengths and challenges. However, with early diagnosis, proper support, and effective intervention, children with autism can learn to manage their emotions and develop positive social skills to navigate social situations successfully.

instruction: Create a 5 day itinerary for a trip to Japan. Include visits to famous locations in Japan, and include a day-by-day breakdown of some activities to do and sites to visit.
reference: Day 1: Arrive at Osaka, in the center of Japan's main Honshu island, and home to a bustling nightlife and many food options. In the morning, visit Osaka castle in the heart of the city, to experience the history of Japan's Edo period. In the afternoon, you can visit either Osaka aquarium Kaiyukan, once the largest aquarium in the world, or get tickets to go to Universal Studios Osaka, which has many themed attractions. At night, pay a visit to Dotonbori, Osaka's famous food alley with a variety of small bites and restaurants. Day 2: Visit Kyoto, Japan's cultural center and former capital. In the morning, visit the Fushimi Inari-taisha shrine, famous worldwide for its orange gates and trail that span almost 4 km. After the visit, explore the old town at the base of the shrine, and head over to Kiyomizu-dera, a famous Buddhist temple which offers stunning views and historical artifacts. In the afternoon and evening, pay a visit to downtown Kyoto, home to department stores and small yet delicious small restaurants. Day 3: Visit Hakone, a famed destination for its hot springs, Mt. Fuji views, and beautiful scenery. Spend some time to visit Lake Ashinoko to see a floating torii gate and expansive views of Mt. Fuji, Japan's tallest peak, visit the sulphur springs where the sulphur cooks chicken eggs so that they become black, then relax in the many hot springs around the region. Hakone is also known for its many ryokans, which are Japanese-style bed and breakfast inns often paired with hot spring onsens. Day 4-5: Spend the last two days in Tokyo, the heart of Japan and the most populated metropolitan area in the world. Tokyo offers many destinations, including the nightlife-heavy districts of Shinjuku and Roppongi, the shopping and fashion centers of Ginza and Harajuku, to the quirky and anime-filled area of Akihabara. Some famous attractions to hit in the city include the Senso-ji temple, Ueno park, Tokyo Skytree, Shibuya crossing, Tsukiji market, and the Imperial Palace.

instruction: Write an argument for keeping public lands under federal control in the Intermountain West.
reference: Public lands make up a huge proportion of the region between the crest of the Sierra Nevada and the Continental Divide in the Rockies, also known as the Intermountain West, and most of these lands are owned by the Federal government. Many residents of this sparsely populated region resent the control of these lands by distant bureaucrats whose regulations place significant restrictions on how the land is used. For this reason, movements have been ongoing for many years to work for the transfer of those lands to local authorities. While this sense of disenfranchisement is understandable, the truth is that local residents would suffer more from the loss of centralized management of these lands than they would gain through local control. This region is mostly desert, a landscape and ecosystem that is unusually vulnerable to degradation. Without the concerted efforts of an administration that can apply consistent regulation and stewardship of these lands across a broad territory that crosses state boundaries, the value of these lands to local residents would decline even further, becoming less productive and less attractive to the hunters, fishermen, and other tourists whose spending represents the majority of income for many of these Intermountain communities.

instruction: My back hurts when I ski a lot of moguls and bumps, why does this happen?

One potential cause to back pain when you ski moguls or bumps is if you are using your back to take the majority impact and absorbing the bump instead of your knee and hip. As you are hitting a bump, you want to keep your back as straight as possible and let your hip and knee take the impact. The movement pattern is similar to squatting down, where you want to drop your bottom down towards your ankle. The reason you want your knee and hip to take the impact is because those joints have much bigger range of motion compared to your back so as you hit a bump or mogul, those joints will help absorb the majority of the irregularity in the terrain so your back is not needing to move as much which will help reduce the strain being put on it.

instruction: Running a business is tough and there will always be problems in the market. Make the case to a skeptical colleague as to why private sector managers should devote attention and energy to being a steward of the institutions of capitalism. Please include citations for Jonathan Haidt.
reference: To steward means to take care of, to guide, and it implies a sense of responsibility. I agree with the notion that, in addition to stories about capitalism prevailing as either an extractor or savior, a third story can be written of “prosperity with problems” in which participants are grateful for accomplishments yet pursuing improvements (Haidt, J.) Putting that together, then, who is responsible for writing this story? I believe that answer to be business leaders themselves -- or else be beholden to government regulation to steward the institution in the direction that benefits not just owners and shareholders, but all stakeholders including employees and the environment. But why should business leaders steward the market? Private managers hold a moral obligation to those relying on capitalism for work and health insurance to create sustainable jobs. As individuals count on business leaders to respond to our world’s most prevalent issues, business leaders also hold a social obligation to do so with care. This response also assigns the appropriate accountability to whomever is responsible for perpetuating a system – if business leaders want to reap the rewards of profit, they must assume responsibility for the very conditions which benefit them. As alluded to above, private interests sometimes conflict horribly with what society and individuals need, so government regulators must be stewards alongside business leaders. instruction: Write a story about a budding romance between two people. Talk about their going on an adventure together where they sneak into a fancy garden in Washington DC and get into just the right amount of trouble.
reference: Natalie and I woke up the morning after a fun night out. I was in DC that week for a work trip, and had extended my stay the weekend before and after, so we could spend time together. We'd only met a month prior, and after more than four weeks of long-distance text message exchanges, it was exciting to finally be together in person. Our first date had been the weekend before, when we'd gone to a Jimmy Buffett concert. It was a magical night. It was now 10am on the Saturday after the work week, and we were ready for another adventure. Natalie, being from DC, wanted to show me the Dumbarton Oaks Gardens, so off we went. Unfortunately, when we got there, the front gates were closed. Still feeling adventurous, we decided to walk around the property, convinced we'd find an unlocked gate, door, or other way to get in. Towards the back end of the property, while we didn't find an open gate, we did find one that was scale-able. And that's exactly what we did. We climbed over that fence, and welcomed ourselves to the beautiful gardens. It was early august, and so much was still in bloom. The gardens were empty, and we thought we had the whole place to ourselves. But, we soon found that that wasn't the case. While exploring a small cottage that also seemed to double as an art gallery, we noticed a small pool right next to it. We also noticed someone swimming in that pool. Presumably that person noticed us too, because a few minutes later a security guard came walking up to us while we were inspecting some fine smelling roses nearby. It was too late to run away, so instead we walked up to the security guard, and thanked him for finding us. As they escorted us out, we complimented them on the great state of the garden, though that didn't seem to calm him down much. He was far too frustrated with the situation. As they were about to lead us out through the front gate, we offered to pay for our admission. They rather sternly refused, and insisted we leave immediately, which we did. And that's how Natalie and I got our free tour of the gardens, and took one step closer to falling in love. Three years later, we were married.

instruction: How many angels can dance on the head of a pin?

instruction: Can you write me a page long essay on whether capitalism needs to be reexamined and amended? Is such a reexamination one of incremental or transformational change? If so, why? If not, why not?
reference: How can I fully participate in a capitalistic society without examining it in the first place? That is the necessary first step to then “re-examine” capitalism, which I unequivocally support. Blindly following a belief, even an economic one, without critically assessing it can run the danger of making me complicit in contributing to the consequences of that belief even without any intent. I can only fully speak from my experience, so that is the lens through which I approach this class; on the larger scale, however, a re-examination is also called for to discern whether capitalism is the best course of action in the long term. Upon this re-examination, I conclude that capitalism is not broken: it is functioning as intended, to create economic value for the majority groups who popularized it. Capitalism in the United States has achieved such fast-paced progress because Black slaves, minority immigrants, and unpaid domestic laborers have assumed the lion’s share of building the system, and the legacies of these systems result in the inequities of race, class, and gender as discussed in class. Such inequities are not only shameful, but plainly unnecessary to continue making such strides in industry, health, longevity, and sharing of ideas. Therefore, capitalism should be amended so that workers more equitably reap the fruits of their labor. Exorbitant CEO pay and the distribution of the majority of profits towards shareholders; global factories which exploit children while imposing unclean and unsafe working conditions on many; unfettered production decimating the planet – should all be amended. Capitalism has grown automation, technology, and AI as well as the development and sharing of thought to remarkable levels. Such progress can be leveraged to address these issues and more. This isn’t idealistic or wishful thinking; though economic situations can seem like “given” circumstances, they are not to be taken for granted; capitalism is a human institution which requires human participation to uphold them. Therefore, capitalism also can be amended. Introducing another consideration is not a limitation on profits; rather, considering additional parameters inspires innovation, as embraced by many leading organizations. But at what pace shall capitalism be amended? The modern United States has necessary checks and balances in the legal systems to uphold the laws and enforce the regulations, which makes me believe that change should be incremental as to learn from our past and carefully curate a new future. It takes time to engage the partners vital to change – academics, politicians, social leaders, business leaders – and transformative change may leave some key stakeholders behind. Over time, incremental change is transformative and can achieve the changes imagined above.

instruction: In football, if touchdowns is the main way to get points, why can't the quarterback always throw the ball to the end zone every time?

instruction: What makes a good teacher?
reference: Throughout history ‘what makes a good teacher?’ has constantly been questioned by both parents and children. Many consider a good teacher to be one who is caring, helpful, yet also strict when necessary. One book that focuses on what makes a good teacher is Our day out, by Willy Russel. The book provided people in the 1970s with a perspective on what both children and parents were looking for, inspiring many British teachers. According to Russel, a good teacher cares for the learning of their students and demonstrates it. If a teacher does not demonstrate caring behavior, their students will sense it. Carol, one of the students says to Mr.Briggs “Don't lie, you! I know you hate me. I've seen you goin' home in your car, passin' us on the street. You hate all the kids.” (Russell 48). Carol believes that Mr. Briggs does not care about his students, even though he does as shown earlier in the book: “Briggs: What? About you? Listen ... if I didn't care, why am I here, now, trying to stop you doing something stupid.” (Russell 48). Mr Briggs believes that caring for students implies also disciplining them at times. “Listen, I'm not going to spend any more time arguing with you. You may have organized this visit, but I'm the one who's been sent by the Headmaster to supervise. Now, either you take control of the children in your charge or I'll be forced to abandon this visit and order everyone home.” Thus, even if a teacher cares about their students, they should demonstrate it. Opinions from students of different ages will help further illustrate the image of a good teacher. Many people think that a good teacher is primarily kind and loving. However, through multiple interviews it appeared to be only partially true. A good teacher, according to most students, is not overly kind and should apply discipline when needed. For example, 12 year old Monon Mukherjee said that he looks for guidance and ability to teach in a teacher. On the other hand, 40 year old Bilal Aslam looks for discipline and ability to teach. 42 year old Cristian Molina also agrees with the need for discipline, however he also expects teachers to feel an urge to help students no matter who they are. The book and the interviews intersect in many ways. They both highlight the importance of kindness, caring for learning, and teacher’s ability to discipline. However, they also differ in important ways. In the book, teachers were encouraged to be kind and apply discipline when necessary, but through the interviews it has been shown that providing help and guidance are also expected in a good teacher. In conclusion, a good teacher cares about their students' learning, is prepared to help them, yet also disciplines them when necessary. A good teacher should feel an urge to teach students and guide them through the complex path of life.

instruction: With the rise of large language models, ChatGPT has changed the way many people work, and AI is getting more and more powerful. Will it eventually replace humans?

I think ChatGPT is likely to follow the same path. By then, it was hard for me to imagine how far AI could go, but now I think the biggest concern is that people are becoming addicted to using ChatGPT. instruction: Why does my chicken create so much liquid when cooked in the skillet?

instruction: What do I need to know about drones to become a hobbyist drone pilot?

As a recreational drone pilot you can capture and immortalize the incredible views experienced in nature while engaging in many outdoor activities. Many also engage in racing and building highly customized high speed drones using first person view (FPV) goggles to fly against other pilots in a close loop course. Before engaging in this fun and rewarding activity there are many rules that a drone pilot must be aware of in order to safely and legally operate your drone. These rules do not apply to racing drones in sanctioned races but do apply to all drones flown in public airspace. All drones over 0.55lbs or 250g need to be registered through the FAA website and can not weigh over 55lbs. If you plan to fly your drone over highly populated areas such as towns, sporting events, or concerts you will need to check local rules and ordinances that require special local licensing, insurance, or approvals. Many higher end drones come with automated software that provides a geospatial mapping software in their interface that lets you know if you are flying in any restricted areas. These include airports, helipads, government facilities, wildlife sanctuaries, etc. All hobbyist drone pilots must follow two main rules. You can never fly above 400 feet and regardless of range you must keep the drone within line of sight. You are completely responsible for any damage your drone causes in the event of loss of control that results in a crash. Lastly, use common sense and don’t invade others' personal space or to invade others’ personal privacy. Staying within these guidelines can provide a joyful and rewarding experience for those who both fly and view the content produced by this hobby and will ensure our ability to do so into the future.

instruction: Which is more important, Nature or Nurture?
reference: The Nature vs Nurture argument has existed for as long as humans have been able to consider complex thought. The debate as to whether the nature (the intrinsic nature, the attitude, or the predisposition), or the nurture (the care, the teachings, or the conditioning) of a child is more responsible for who or what they become in adult life. Largely it is considered that humans are a product of context (Nurture). The situations in which we are raised have a considerable bearing on who we become in later life. But, it's not necessarily so black and white. There are countless examples of children having been born into extremely difficult circumstances, who have grown to be well rounded, high contributing members of society. As a result, It would be reasonable to assume that Nature is a strong factor, regardless of the Nurture (the environment) in which a person is raised. After all, there's no guarantee that someone growing up in an abusive household will then abuse others themselves. So then is Nature more important? The difficulty with the debate is that no one individual is the same as another. Experiments to establish the efficacy of Nature vs Nurture are difficult to perform. Not only from a human rights perspective, but additionally from a variable standpoint as well. Really there are far too many variables to control with regards to human nature, that any imposition of control on the Nurture element would be imbalanced. When considering this question, it's important to recognise that developmental psychology is still in its early stages, and to understand that both Nature AND Nurture are necessary factors in human development.

instruction: what method of commuting works best to get from Marin County to downtown San Francisco?
reference: There are many ways to get from Marin County to downtown San Francisco. You can drive a car, which can be fast in the morning, taking, say, 45 minutes or less if you leave before 8am. Driving home, however, can take up to an hour and a half or more depending on traffic. You can take a bus, which generally takes about an hour and fifteen minutes either way. You can also take a bicycle to a bus stop, and the bus will carry your bike, but the spaces for bikes can fill up before you get on the bus, so check the route before trying this method. Ferries that take you from Larkspur to the Ferry Building are also very popular. You can drive to the ferry landing, park your car, and get on the ferry to downtown San Francisco. When the weather is nice, this can be a wonderful way to either unwind or catch up on work. Ferries can be subject to weather delays and cancellations, so check the weather before trying this method. Finally, you can take a bicycle or even run all the way in to downtown San Francisco from Marin County. Bicycling is generally an hour to hour and a half round trip, but again check the weather and your fitness level before committing to this. And most of all, make sure you eat enough calories during the day to fuel that ride home! There are some intrepid souls who have taken to the water and swam from Cavallo Point to Aquatic Park, which takes a lot of practice and planning. instruction: Tell me three key things to do to drive a car faster on a track
reference: Driving a car on a track can be an exhilarating experience, but there a few rules to keep in mind. Here are three key things to remember: 1. Eyes up - Many drivers have a tendency to look directly at the end of the hood or at the next cone or apex. Keep your eyes up and to be able to assess where you want to go. 2. Look where you want to go - Your hands on the steering wheel follow your eyes, so look where you want to go, not what you want to avoid or navigate. For example. you should be looking at the exit of a turn as you enter the turn (or the apex if it's a wide turn) 3. Slow in, fast out - Cornering can be particularly tricky, because we tend to turn in too fast and too early, which can set up for a slow exit. Brake hard, take it slow, and wait to turn into a corner to best position you and the car to accelerate swiftly out of the turn.

instruction: Why is my buttercream frosting not white?

Pure white buttercream does not exist, as the color of butter is slightly yellow, which will give your buttercream frosting a small amount of color. However, the most likely culprit of your tan buttercream is your traditional vanilla extract.

instruction: I need a short film script that can be produced on a low budget. Here is the concept: kids follow a trail of birdhouses through the woods only to find a mega birdhouse inhabited by a monstrous witch of some kind. The working title is Birds and the Beast. Create a brief script of the scene right before the kids go into the large birdhouse (less than 400 words), and include dialogue between the three main characters and descriptions of the setting.
reference: BIRDS AND THE BEAST (Script) [Setting: Dusk; three teenagers (Billy, Amanda, and Josh) are cautiously walking through the foggy woods following a path of crudely constructed birdhouses, unsure of where they might lead to.] Billy: “Don’t you think we should turn around?” Amanda: “Come on, are you scared?” Billy: “Obviously! This is undoubtedly the creepiest thing I have ever seen!” Amanda: “No way, we’ve all seen Josh’s mom in her avocado face mask.” Josh: “Would you guys shut up? I’d rather we didn’t make a ton of noise out here.” Amanda: “You’re scared, too?! Man, I’m surrounded by wimps! Plus, I can barely hear anything over all these birds chirping.” Billy: “Those don’t sound like chirps to me—I think they’re crying.” Amanda: “Birds don’t cry, idiot.” Josh: “Yeah, and they don’t burp, either.” Billy: “What does that have to do with anything?” Josh: “Nothing, I guess, except fun facts always make me feel better—“ [Amanda interrupts Josh after a bone-chilling creak comes from beyond the trees.] Amanda: “Did you hear that? Something is out there.” Billy: “Well, look who’s scared now!” Amanda: “I’m serious—shut up.” [The group stops walking and listens.] Amanda: “Look over there.” [Amanda points across a marshy area of the forest to an enormous version of the birdhouses they had been following. The large birdhouse was constructed at ground level in a grove of aspen trees, and moss had begun to take over the white wood it was made from.] [The group shared a look, then each of them waited for someone else to speak first and come up with a plan. Finally, Josh broke the silence.] Josh: “That thing is huge, but it seems abandoned.” Amanda: “Of course it’s abandoned. Who would occupy it—a 15-foot-tall bird?” Billy: “15-feet-tall?! I don’t even want to find out!” Amanda: “But we came all this way! What good is this story if we turn around now? Everyone will think I’m a wimp, just like the two of you! No way I’m letting that happen. I’m going closer.” [Amanda stormed off away from the group. Billy and Josh reluctantly followed, both wanting to avoid being cast as cowardice in the story Amanda would tell once they got back to summer camp.]

instruction: Can you write a short story about a rabbit drinking a can of soda for the first time? The sugar and caffeine would make it hop fast!
reference: Once upon a time, there was a boy named Kyle. Kyle owned a pet rabbit name Hip and loved it a lot. He would play with it a lot, feed it, have it hop around his room, and plenty of other things as well. One normal day, Kyle had to go to school and waved goodbye to Hip. Kyle left a can of soda next to Hip's cage, and Hip decided it wanted to try some. He ran to the side of the cage with the soda and crashed into it, knocking both the cage and the soda down. The door to the cage was open, and the imitation hay was spilled all across the room. The soda spilled across the room as well. Hip was able to get up just fine and he noticed the soda spill. Hip hopped over to the spill and started licking up the soda. Maybe it was his way of cleaning up his mess. But something started to change with Hip. Hip was feeling a little jittery. The caffeine in the can started to take effect, and Hip was hopping around the room a lot more than normal. He was moving twice as fast. The satisfaction from drinking the sugary drink made Hip hop twice as high! As high as the bed frame! Hip hopped on top of the bed and found a very cozy place to rest his legs. He didn't notice the rabbit feet markings on the covers or the ground. Hip was just happy he got to drink the soda. He tried jumping on the bed, and he found out that he could jump even higher on the bed! This was new territory for Hip! The feeling of being in the air for so long was refreshing, and Hip wanted to do it more. But Hip knew this wouldn't last. The mess that he made for Kyle was too much. The rabbit started to sulk and tire. All that jumping made him tired. He decided it was time to rest and recover. Hip had to wait for Kyle to clean up his mess. Either way, the experience that Hip had was amazing, and He will never forget it.

instruction: I’m trying to write a scene, but I have a plot ready. Please help me write a scene where David has been waiting for seven hours since he placed a note in Betty's desk, and when he suddenly hears a noise coming from the desk, he discovers that the note he placed there is gone. He is shocked and unable to understand how this could be possible. David decides to stay in the room until he gets answers. Two hours later, he hears a swishing noise and sees pieces of material swirling in the air, eventually forming into Betty. She is unconscious, and David rushes to her side. Gradually, the color returns to her face, and she regains consciousness. Betty asks David if he loves her, and he confirms that he does, taking a moment to tuck a stray curl behind her ear. The scene should be under 400 words and there should be dialogues between these characters.
reference: David seats himself in an antique chair in the corner of the room. It’s been 7 hours since he placed the note on the desk. As he leans back in the chair thinking about the reality of this, he unexpectedly hears a noise coming from the desk. He leans forward listening, but hears nothing else. He walks silently to the desk. Opening the cover, then the drawer, he’s shocked. The note he put in there is gone. Staggering backward he leans over taking a deep breath. Standing, he runs his fingers through his hair in utter bewilderment. Pacing back and forth in front of the desk, he begins reasoning with himself. I’m here, and I don’t see anyone else. How can this be? He stands gaping at the desk. Walking back to the chair, he decides he will not move an inch from this room until he gets answers. Two hours later, he hears a swishing noise. He sits straight up in the chair and watches in astonishment as pieces of the material circle into the wind settling to the floor. Once the pieces merge, he sees it’s Betty. Running to her quickly, he finds her unconscious. He picks her head up and cradles it in his arms. Staring at her he sees she’s pale. Gradually her face returns to normal. Calling her name, her eyes flutter open. “David, is that you?” “Yes, my love. I’m here.” Closing her eyes, she lies silent. “Betty, are you okay? Talk to me.” Opening her eyes again she replies, “Yes. I’m okay. It takes a while for me to gain strength from the travel. Just give me a minute. Each trip gets harder and harder to come out of the daze.” Leaning down to kiss her lips gently, he says, “It’s okay, take your time. I’ll wait.” After about 15 minutes, she gets the strength to sit up. Holding her forehead, she abates the nausea. Taking deep breaths, she feels herself returning to normal. David helps her up. Their eyes meet. Rachel asks, “You love me?” Surprised to hear that is the first thing she says coming out of her tranced state, he laughs. “Yes, Rachel, I do.” He moves her over to a settee. Seated beside her, he takes the curl falling in her face and pushes it behind her ear.

instruction: Oh, great computer in the sky, can you explain the difference between a high wing and a low wing on airplanes? Why would one be preferable rather than the other? Why haven’t aircraft designers settled on a certain type that’s best?
reference: There are a lot of engineering considerations that go into wing design. Different styles excel in certain situations but not in others, so there’s no one perfect design. The best configuration for a lightweight bush plane won't necessarily be the best for a massive airliner. Plus, high and low wings are not the only options. Here are a few of the key advantages and disadvantages that may help illustrate the situation: - All other things being equal, a plane with low wings will have a shorter takeoff roll thanks to the ground effect. - The engine placement and wing placement are linked. Only large planes such as jet airliners can fit their engines in pods below a low wing. This placement makes it easy for maintenance crews to access the engine components, so it speeds up repairs. Smaller low-wing aircraft must carry their engines elsewhere; though the planes are shorter overall, that still often places the engines out of immediate reach to ground crews. - Mounting engines low on a low wing does, however, increase the likelihood of ingesting foreign object debris (FOD) during takeoff or landing that can damage the engine. Some designs like the US Air Force’s C-17 mitigate this by mounting engines on high wings. - High wings are inherently more roll-stable. Since their center of mass hangs below the center of lift, these planes are unlikely to experience unexpected or uncontrollable rolling motion. It does mean they require more force to generate an intentional roll force, though. - In small aircraft, low wings limit ground visibility but improve overall visibility in the air. High wings do the opposite. - Small low-wing aircraft can be hard for passengers to enter and exit. - A high-mounted wing usually leaves more available cargo space in the fuselage than a low-mounted wing. - Because the wings are closer to the ground, the landing gear on low-wing designs usually require less structure and reinforcement. - In-wing fuel tanks in a high-mounted wing can use gravity to feed fuel to the engines; low-wing tanks need fuel pumps. However, high wings are harder to refuel. - High-wing aircraft are more heavily affected by crosswinds than low-wing ones.

instruction: Write me the interaction of a hero who learns that the villain is them from the future who time-traveled back to the present. Make sure to include some elements of magic and make it in a civil war setting. I want the hero to be trapped by the villain, and is talking to them through a prison cell. Make it in the perspective of the hero. This is supposed to be in the middle of a story, so don't bother with introducing her or the setting, it is assumed that those were introduced earlier in the story. reference: It's been about a week since I was captured by the enemy. They sealed my magic away and I feel my strength deteriorating. Am I gonna die in this cell? I hope someone rescues me soon. "Hello," says a mysterious woman. "Who are you?" I reply. I didn't even detect her presence. "I am you," she says. "What?" I question. "How can you be me? I am me; there is no other me." "I came from the future. I am here to make sure the rebellion wins," she states. I can't believe this. How can she say that she is me? Does time travel exist? I've heard of time-stopping magic, but that is incredibly rare and widely considered a myth. Although taking a closer look at her, I guess I can see some resemblances. NO! I can't just nonchalantly believe she is me! This must be some trick. "I want you to join me," interrupts the mysterious woman. "I know this is a lot to handle right now, but I can assure you that I am you. I even know your deepest darkest secret that you peed yourself until you were fourteen!" "What," I reply, still in shock. "There's no way, who told you? Was it my childhood friend Fred? I knew he wouldn't keep his mouth shut after I told his parents that he was sneaking out of his room while he was grounded." "Ah Fred, I loved Fred. No, he didn't tell on you. I know because I am you," insists the mysterious woman. "I still don't believe you, I can never believe the obvious lie that you are me from the future," I assert, still trying to get a hold of this situation. She can't be me! I fight for the kingdom, not some sort of rebellion! There is no way I would switch sides! No, this must be a lie. I just have to stay true to what I know. I will get out of this situation eventually. Right? "Well, I remember it taking a little while for you to trust me, I guess I will leave you to reflect a little. I'll be back tomorrow. instruction: Create a guided meditation prompt focused on the healing power of nature. It should include the following scenes: a lush forest, a flower-filled meadow, a babbling brook, and a clear, sunny sky. The focus should be on relieving stress and anxiety. The first paragraph will only be able preparative breathing and freeing the mind.
reference: Close your eyes and empty your mind. Free your thoughts and focus only on your breathing. Take a deep breath to the count of 4, 1-2-3-4, and release to the count of 4, 1-2-3-4. Repeat this two more times feeling the tension flowing down from the top of your head out the soles of your feet. Picture yourself walking barefoot in a lush forest filled with strong trees. These trees hold so much life and provide clean air for you to breathe. Touch the tree and feel the life flow from its bark through the palms of your hands. Take a deep breath embracing the gift of strength it gives and releasing the feeling of weakness as you release this breath. You continue your path through the forest and come to a babbling brook. You take a small step into the water feeling its coolness between your toes. You continue to walk deeper into the water allowing it to wash over your entire body cleansing every inch of your being, renewing your energy at the atomic level. Open your mouth and feel it refreshing you from the inside out. Take a deep breath welcoming the renewal it gives and releasing self-doubt and blame. As you reach the other side of the brook witness the breathtaking sight before you; a meadow filled with beautiful flowers as far as your eye can see. You gaze up at the clear sky, basking in the warmth of the sun. Take a deep breath allowing it to recharge your core and release fatigue and weariness. Lay down in the field and allow the fragrance of the flowers to envelope you. Light, fresh lavender mixed with sweet notes of vanilla invade your nostrils demanding a calmness to settle within you. Let go of all your anxiety. Nothing else matters at this moment. Your mind, body, and spirit are renewed. Open your eyes and give yourself a few moments to acknowledge your new mindset. Continue to take deep breaths as you prepare to start or end your day. Go forward with the positivity you've instilled.

instruction: Write a tl:dr review of this book review in the voice of a Gen X mom talking to her Gen Z daughter: Title: The Knockoff Author: Lucy Sykes and Jo Piazza ISBN: 9780385539586 No. of Pages: 352 Genre: Contemporary Fiction Origins: Doubleday Release Date: 19 May 2015 Synopsis: “An outrageously stylish, wickedly funny novel of fashion in the digital age, The Knockoff is the story of Imogen Tate, editor in chief of Glossy magazine, who finds her twentysomething former assistant Eve Morton plotting to knock Imogen off her pedestal, take over her job, and reduce the magazine, famous for its lavish 768-page September issue, into an app. When Imogen returns to work at Glossy after six months away, she can barely recognize her own magazine. Eve, fresh out of Harvard Business School, has fired “the gray hairs,” put the managing editor in a supply closet, stopped using the landlines, and hired a bevy of manicured and questionably attired underlings who text and tweet their way through meetings. Imogen, darling of the fashion world, may have Alexander Wang and Diane von Furstenberg on speed dial, but she can’t tell Facebook from Foursquare and once got her iPhone stuck in Japanese for two days. Under Eve’s reign, Glossy is rapidly becoming a digital sweatshop—hackathons rage all night, girls who sleep get fired, and “fun” means mandatory, company-wide coordinated dances to Beyoncé. Wildly out of her depth, Imogen faces a choice—pack up her Smythson notebooks and quit, or channel her inner geek and take on Eve to save both the magazine and her career. A glittering, uproarious, sharply drawn story filled with thinly veiled fashion personalities, The Knockoff is an insider’s look at the ever-changing world of fashion and a fabulous romp for our Internet-addicted age.” To say that the two clash is an understatement. Imogen struggles to learn the new rules of doing business to capitalize on the available technology, while Eve just wants Imogen out of the way. The dynamic between the two is fraught with tension and frustration and achingly realistic. Talk to anyone in management above a certain age, and they will all have stories similar to Imogen’s. Then again, talk to anyone Eve’s age and her frustrations are their frustrations. The Knockoff captures the individual sides perfectly. There is a lot to love in The Knockoff. Think of it as The Devil Wears Prada for the next generation. However, to expect the same story as Prada would be to seriously underestimate the twists and turns The Knockoff has in store for readers. Anyone who has ever been frustrated at work due to a genuine clash in personality and expectations should read The Knockoff. In fact, it would make a fantastic book club option, as it is quick, light, and humorous, and yet presents multiple situations and characters that are open to interpretation.
reference: No worries, dear! The Knockoff made me laugh, and I think you'll get a kick out of it for very different reasons. Authors Lucy Sykes and Jo Piazza describe the clash between a Gen X fashion magazine executive back from a six-month leave who discovers that her publication, Glossy, has been turned into an app. The main character, Imogen Tate, is cool and friends with everybody in the fashion world; whereas the 20-something leading the app project - Harvard MB Eve, Imogen's former assistant!- makes her young team of employees works all night and participate in stupid dances, before viciously firing them for trivial reasons. Imogen doesn't have the slightest clue about tech or apps (she's more of a Smythson notebook kind of person) but realizes that she has to learn a few things quickly before Eve destroys everything she has worked to build. No spoilers, but think of it as a sort of updated The Devil Wears Prada. It will make you laugh and might remind you of a few people you know.

instruction: Write a short passage about a bookworm named Hestia going to a bookstore that a kind man named Tom owns, and her feelings when she first enters.
reference: Hestia shifted uncomfortably from one foot to the other, rubbing at her arms. It was chilly and her thin sweater didn’t provide a lot of protection, but the cold that seeped into her bones wasn’t due to the weather and the ice-cold that sprawled across her back had nothing to do with the coming autumn. It was another kind of cold entirely. Gingerly, Hestia walked up the stone steps and into the bookstore. “Just a moment,” Tom called from deep within the dark and gloomy shop. Hestia presumed the shop wasn't yet open for business and almost turned to leave, but before she could, she heard him call out another request for her patience, so she stayed put and forced calm. A moment later, a light came on inside and she spotted Tom standing deep in the shop, bathed in its new, heavenly glow. A soft gasp escaped her. Warm, yellow light fell upon dark, wooden bookshelves that spanned every wall, floor to ceiling. Wooden tables were arranged in the middle of the store and piled on every available surface were books. Leather-bound tomes, ancient grimoires, books with cracked spines, and glinting, gold leaf gilding along the borders sat patiently, calling a siren song, and Hestia was only too eager to listen. Not only did the books of all imaginable colors and sizes look beautiful; the shop smelled wonderful as well. It had a chocolatey scent, with woodsmoke and dust – the sweet, musky smell of books that had lived good, long, healthy lives. If heaven was on earth, Hestia had found it.

instruction: Please write a humorous/ironic script for a speech in a crowdfunding video by a man named Dr. Disaster. He is asking for $500 Million to fund a doomsday device that he calls, "The Crust Cracker 5000," which works by cracking a planet's crust like an egg and exposing the mantle. One paragraph about the general pitch, one about why people will want to donate to make such a thing, and one about what the money will be used for. reference: Hello, I am Dr. Disaster, and this . . . *Dr. Disaster cracks an egg with a spoon* . . . was an egg. That was pretty satisfying, wasn't it? Now imagine how satisfying that would be on a bigger scale. No, bigger than that. That's right, I'm talking about the Earth. Wouldn't it be great if there was a machine that could crack the earth just like an egg? I certainly believe so. That's why I made these plans here . . . *pulls up blueprints for an intricately designed machine* . . . for what I lovingly call the Crust Cracker 5000. Although these are blueprints right now, my team and I are hard at work on the prototype. Unfortunately, doomsday devices aren't cheap. That's why we need your help. We're asking for just $500 Million to help us fund this beautiful machine. Now, I'm no idiot. I'm sure everyone watching this video may be wondering, "Dr. Disaster, why would I want to help fund the production of a machine that would crack the core of the Earth? I live there!" That annoying hangnail that you just can't get rid of right now without feeling like you're tearing off all the skin on your finger? Absolutely obliterated. Literally, any problem you can think of would be solved quickly and humanely with the Crust Cracker 5000. Except for death; but we all die eventually, so why suffer until then? *Dr. Disaster walks in front of a half-built machine with scientists in lab coats around it.* Now, you may be wondering what we will do with your hard-earned money. Where exactly does it go? Let me be the first to assure you that none of it goes into our pockets. We are purely a non-profit organization. Every cent we make is being put directly into the development of the Crust Cracker 5000. For example, let's take a look at this section of our prototype. In my demonstration, the action performed by this piece was done with a spoon. Think of this as a bigger spoon. Unfortunately, Crust Cracker 1 through Crust Cracker 4999 has failed at this point. We just can't get a spoon big enough to generate enough force to crack this planet open. With your money, we could get the tools we need to add to the existing Crust Cracker platform and really get to that good magma goo in the mantle. Again, I have been Dr. Disaster, and this is my crack . . . *Dr. Disaster winks* . . . team of scientists. Thank you so much for your time, and I hope you do consider donating to this wonderful cause.

instruction: Come up with a fictional account about a female housecat who stepped into a time machine and found herself in a 1970s shopping mall, armed only with a charge card. instruction: Write a light-hearted short story about a pink poodle named Polly who feels self-conscious about being pink.
reference: Polly the poodle has pink hair that often makes her stand out in a crowd. She’s the only pink poodle most other dogs have seen, so they often stare or talk about her. It makes Polly feel shy and self-conscious because she doesn’t like the attention. Holly the husky noticed Polly standing away from all of the other dogs and often looking down. That made Holly sad, so she went over to talk to Polly. Holly asked Polly, “Why don’t you come over with our group?” “I feel a little out of place,” Polly answered. “Everyone is looking at me.” “That’s just because you’re so beautiful, Polly,” Holly said. “We’ve never seen a pink poodle, and we are so amazed!” Holly and her friends made Polly realize her difference is what makes her so special. Polly started to perk up and gain confidence. From now on, Polly is going to walk in a room knowing her unique quality makes her beautiful, and that it’s okay to be different.

instruction: write a story about a sad trumpet named after a jazz musician. make it have a happy ending. make it 2 paragraphs. kinda like a children's story.
reference: There was a sad trumpet named Wynton. He had always been a quiet trumpet, shy, and never really made a sound. While the fellow trumpets in the band blasted away with confidence, Wynton remained silent. This made him feel sad and isolated, as the other trumpets didn't seem to want him around. Wynton didn't understand why he couldn't make sounds like the others. He hadn't fallen, and he wasn't missing any parts. One day, Wynton decided to travel out into another trumpet quartet's practice to see if there were others like him. He met a trumpet who blared a happy tune. They all bounced notes off of each other smoothly. Wynton was amazed and inspired by the new band's sounds and started to feel a spark. After a few attempts, he let out a melodic arpeggio. "Doot doot da doodle doot doo doo." The other trumpets congratulated him on his newfound ability. Wynton felt happier than he ever had before. From then on, Wynton blasted out new notes with pride and jammed with his new trumpet friends for hours.

instruction: Write one paragraph about the Tlachihualtepetl pyramid. Keep it at or below 15 sentences. Include its size and when it was built. Also, include any aspects of worship it had. Include aspects of its more recent history, too. Name at least one specific year.
reference: When people hear the word "pyramid," they often think of Egypt. However, the world's largest pyramid is in Cholula, Mexico. Tlachihualtepetl, also called the Great Pyramid of Cholula, is 217 feet (66 meters) tall and its base is 1,476 by 1,1476 feet (450 by 450 meters). Its total volume is 157 million cubic feet. Due to its size, it took centuries to build. It was worked on several different times between 300 BC and 700 AD. There was a temple above it to worship Quetzalcoatl - the Aztec god of learning and books. However, the temple was abandoned around the 8th or 9th century AD. Over time, it became covered with vegetation. As a result, it blended in and Spaniards first mistook it for a hill when they conquered Mexico in 1521. They replaced the temple with a church and the pyramid stayed hidden until the 1930s when the earth started to erode. Archeologists have excavated and studied many parts of the pyramid since then, including the altars. It has also become a tourist attraction since then. Thousands of people visit Tlachihualtepetl each year.

instruction: Write the beginning of a short story about a 32-year-old female librarian named Felicity who has recently discovered she has magical powers. Describe her personality, physical appearance, and hobbies, including that she has an orange cat named Felix. Add that her powers include telekinesis and weather control.
reference: Felicity was a soft-spoken librarian who enjoyed a quiet life with Felix, her ginger cat. When she wasn't working at the library, Felicity enjoyed cycling, bowling, and weekly meetings with the local book club. Her friends would describe her as soft-spoken and compassionate. However, shortly after her 32nd birthday, Felicity's life was turned upside down. Suddenly, objects started moving around on their own, seeming to come to her at the first thought of need. Even stranger, the weather seemed to reflect her moods perfectly. After a few days of odd happenings, Felicity turned to her trusty books to find an answer. Although she felt a bit ridiculous looking for books about magic and witchcraft as a rational, modern-day woman, it seemed to be her only option. Surely there must be some truth in the old tales. Finally, after weeks of searching, Felicity stumbled across a rare collection of 18th-century grimoires. These otherworldly tomes sent a shiver up her spine, but she knew that inside one of them lay the key to understanding why this was happening to her. When she brought home the stack of ancient books, Felicity set them down on her end table with a sigh. She couldn't fathom where to begin her search. Then, with a slight growl, Felix jumped up on the table, knocked the stack of books to the floor, walked straight to the one titled The Magus, and sat on the cover. It was almost as if he was trying to tell her something. With a shake of her head, Felicity picked up the book her cat seemed to have chosen, mumbling to herself that it was as good a place to start as any. But she couldn't shake the feeling that Felix was watching her expectantly for the rest of the evening.

instruction: I'm having some trouble getting my preteen to understand the importance of good hygiene practices like bathing, brushing teeth et cetera. He doesn't see why he should do these things because he's "not interested in lame girls like his dodo-brain brother." Write a letter to him from B.O. (body odor) leveling with him and explaining the science behind staying clean. His name is Brett and he loves playing Roblox.
reference: Dear Brett, What up my man? I'm so happy we met a few years ago but I need to talk to you about the dangers of keeping me around too long. Listen, I know just how much of a drag bathing and brushing your teeth can be. I mean, shouldn't we be leveling up on Roblox instead? Of course, we should but if we don't take care of our bodies in the meantime, we may not be able to play the game for much longer. The reason body odor is so foul is because bacteria are feeding on your sweat and dead skill cells in those areas. If we don't wash them daily, we set our skin up for a losing battle. With each passing day, the bacteria warriors will increase and they'll be able to wage stronger attacks on your skin until they break through and create an infection. Our skin is the biggest barrier we have against bacteria present in the world. One of the ways you can keep it strong and healthy is to clean it daily. A similar thing happens when you don't brush your teeth twice a day, only way worse. When we eat sometimes food particles get trapped between our teeth and near our gumline. These tiny particles are like a buffet to hungry bacteria and they'll feed and grow until they become strong enough to attack the enamel on your teeth. They link together and create this thick barrier called plaque and they'll use it to break down your enamel and create little holes in your teeth called cavities. Cavities don't just go away on their own. You'll need to see a dentist and if you don't they'll just keep getting bigger and bigger until the whole tooth is in danger of dying and falling out. Unlike its younger siblings the baby teeth, permanent teeth are the end of the line and you won't get new ones to replace those that fall out. I only want what's best for you dude and I want to see you ruin your body by being lazy. Just brush your teeth twice a day and take a bath daily and you'll be happy and healthy for a very long time. Until next time, Your pal B.O.

instruction: Write me the beginning of an article on planned obsolescence. Include the fact that car parts are built to fail after a certain amount of time and that Phones become obsolete because they are no longer supported, not because they don't work. Please use a studious tone
reference: Is it time to end planned obsolescence? I first came across the term, ‘planned obsolescence while I was studying to become a mechanic (a course I passed but ultimately never pursued) Everything on a traditional car is built to a certain specification so that it will fail after a certain amount of miles. A clutch every 70,000 to 100,000 miles. A cambelt every 40,000 and so on. It struck me as strange at the time. Why not just build all the parts to last? But it makes some sense on a car at least. I mean the whole thing is full of moving parts and wear and tear is unavoidable over several thousand miles. But other than a cracked screen, I have never seen an iPhone or Samsung crumble in its owner's hand due to too many hours spent in a pocket. The truth is the iPhone 5 I have in my kitchen drawer works just as well as it did on the day I bought it. It's just that Apple decided to stop supporting it. Apps could be made to still function on it. But it's costly to support several generations of a phone both for the manufacturer and anyone that wants to create apps for either iOS or Android. Not to mention, if you are using a five or six-generation old phone you haven't put any money in Apple's pocket for quite some time.

instruction: I want you to write a narrative with a bleak, depressing tone about an office worker who is overworked and dislikes his lifestyle. Give me more than 300 words. Make it third person. Don't include dialogue. Introduce another character right at the end.
reference: Maurice walked home in the dark after work. He'd been up since before the sun had risen and was stuck in the office the entire day. His only chance to see the sunlight was on a trip between office floors. He'd gotten to bask in the sun for a few minutes while waiting for the elevator. As he shuffled down the street heading home, he wondered how long it would keep up. He had been single since graduating high school. He started working right out of college. He had been promoted once, but even with all his money life didn't seem any brighter. What was there to spend the money on? He stopped by a Mcdonald's on the way home and grabbed something for dinner. The night shift recognized him. They chatted a bit while he waited for his food, but it made him feel worse. How often had he gone there at night? How many times did he have to go there for them to have become accustomed to him? He ate his fries out of the bag on his way home but stopped in a park and finished his food on the bench there. He couldn't bring himself to take the food home. What was the point in living this lifestyle where work consumed his life, and no one waited for him at home? Something had to change, and it needed to change soon. He could go drinking, but drinking alone was worse than just going home. He could go to a girl's bar, of course, and be surrounded by beautiful women while drinking and venting his troubles. However, it was just a job to them. They didn't care one bit about his problems or who he was. Maurice sighed and stared at the moon for a time before a woman entered the park, sitting on the swing and crying.

instruction: Write a story from the perspective of a pickle as it is going from a cucumber in the field to being jarred and put away for the year.
reference: I am a pickle. Well, no that isn't quite right, I'm a cucumber right now but soon I will be a pickle. Days ago some friendly hands picked me up from my nice sunny patch in the field. I was about ready to come in, to be honest, the heat was getting to me and there were far too many rabbits lurking around. It was very nice to be carried inside, given a nice cool bath, and set aside for the night to sleep and relax. I woke up a bit later than usual still surrounded in the colander by my other cucumber friends. They were still sleeping so I did my best not to disturb them. They weren't a talkative bunch normally anyway. The sun was just starting to peak in through the curtains above the sink when a lady entered the room. The same lady who grabbed me from the patch yesterday. She seemed very friendly and nice. At least I thought so until she picked me up, bowl and all, and gave me a big shake. What a way to rise and shine. I could hear the other cucumbers grumbling too. She transported us a few feet away to another part of the countertop. Then, the lady mixed a bunch of ingredients in a big pot on the stove and it started to smell good but it also tickled my nose a bit. Perhaps a bit too garlicky for my tastes. Next thing I knew she was picking me up again but this time she stuck me in a jar! I couldn't believe it, it was finally happening! It's the most exciting day in any gherkins life. A few of my other cucumber friends joined me and we all nestled up close to each other. It was very cozy and everyone had a nice view through the glass too. Then, the nice lady gave us a warm bath. It felt even nicer than the cool bath I had before. It had hints of dill and pepper and it covered me from my tippy toes all the way to the top of my head. She put a nice little roof over top sealing me in. And I knew that from this day forward I was a cucumber no more, now I was one proud pickle.

instruction: Draft a book review of “The Lorax” and pretend you were a fancy critic with picky taste in children’s books.
reference: Title: Review of “The Lorax”: Real or Imaginary? As a highly respected children’s literature critic, I know I had to dive into Dr. Seuss’ “The Lorax” with a mix of curiosity and skepticism. I, of course, have to be honest and say I definitely had my doubts about whether or not the book would still stand the test of time for today’s children. But as I read each and every page, I was able to find a certain kind of depth in this story that went far beyond funny pictures and words. If any of my readers are unfamiliar with the plotline, the Lorax is a mustachioed creature who is the environment’s protector. He speaks out against the Once-ler, who represents corporate greed. The truffula trees and bar-ba-loots are endangered, and the Lorax urges others to care. “The Lorax” is more than zany pictures and childish rhymes. It is really a metaphor regarding the environment on Earth. Dr. Seuss deserves some praise for being able to translate a confusing-yet-important topic for children. After all, they say children will inherit the Earth, right?

instruction: Hi can you write a short story about a kid who grew up in the dangerous Bronx but both of his parents are Dalmatians. The story should include the kid exploring the Bronx at night and finding out there is more to the city than what’s in the news. There should be 3 paragraphs and the beginning of each sentence for the paragraphs should spell NYC.
reference: Nighttime in the Bronx isn’t exactly safe. As the daytime exposure dwindles, the misfits of the evening arise. The AM news often reports on matters that happen after the sun sets. The rowdy crowds that break things in a drunken stupor. The robberies and murders take place in the alleys. Hearing such scary news, my parents always barked at me to stay home after dark. Yet being cooped up at home is never fun, especially when you live with your parents, who just happen to be 2 Dalmatians. Sure, it’s fun to throw the ball around with them, but I don’t want to do that the entire time. I’m 14, and I just want to get away from those 2. So, after they fall asleep, I’m going to leave the house and see what the night has to offer. Carefully, I slip out the back door once my parent's light turns off. When I get to the street corner, what I saw amazed me. I expected the streets to be blotted with dim city lights and shadowy figures, but instead, I saw fire walkers, unfazed by the hot rocks they stood upon. There were dancers covered in colorful fabrics waking up and down. Sure, I saw some shady stuff happen, but that doesn’t take away from the levity I saw. The street was filled with life. It was literally night and day, from my expectations. I can’t wait to see what else the city has to offer.

instruction: A boy likes a girl and she comes over to his house. They get along and she has to stay for dinner for some reason. Let's say her name is Jess. The boy shows her his skull collection but it's actually just seeds.
reference: The boy awaits the girl. He fidgets. He's planned everything just right. He wants the afternoon to be perfect. He combed his hair and chose his favorite T-shirt, the striped one. He recalls his mother saying it brings out his eyes. Whatever that means. But Mum's a girl, so he reckons she knows something about what girls like. He has been thinking for a week about what girls like. The girl shows up with a small blue bow on the left side of her hair. The boy thinks she's splendid, though he'd never say so. They play jacks; they play cards. Mum makes them lemonade, then says, "Jess has to stay for dinner; her parents are running late. You two go play in the garden for a while. It's shady, and the boy is glad. She's staying for dinner. He hopes Mum will ask him to set the table. He'll place her sitting next to his. The boy and the girl sit on the rusty garden swing. Time passes. He glances over at her to see how she feels, but he can't tell. She is smiling, so that is something. "You want to see my collection? It's secret," he says. In his room, he pulls the shoebox from under the bed. When he stands, he senses how the girl steps closer. His skin prickles. He places the shoebox on the floor and sits cross-legged in front of it. He looks up at the girl and sees a series of conspiratorial afternoons like this together. His heart pounds when she sits opposite him, the musty box between them. He unwraps the contents, pulling old newspaper and tissue off as carefully as he can. In the bottom sit four small skulls. Dreadful eyes, large and oblong, drooping down. Noses flat and misshapen. Wide moaning mouths. The girl gasps and leans in for a closer inspection. "Careful," he says. "They're haunted." He showed this to his younger sister once, and she ran away screaming. The girl reaches out a light finger to touch the top of one of the skulls. "Can I hold it?" "Maybe next time." At dinner, their secrets fill the space between them. He worries over his small deception. He wonders when he'll tell her that his skulls are only ripe seed pods.

instruction: Write a book review for “Soggy Yellow Spuds,” a book about the fateful journey of a sack of potatoes from farm to factory. Make it a positive review from the point of view of a middle-aged woman. Choose an author name.
reference: **Soggy Yellow Spuds by Ronald A. Spudchaser** is a raw, thought-provoking story of one burlap-wrapped family of young potatoes on an emotional journey across the country. Their courage as they bounce from farm truck to semi-trailer to freight container, trading warm spring sunshine for cavernous metal walls is humbling. At one point in the story, I cried when the bag tore and the smallest potato fell to the ground during a transfer between trucks. My kids are long grown up, but my motherly heart broke. The other spuds could only watch in horror as they rolled away into a gutter. Their stoicism throughout the harrowing tale is a lesson in perseverance and bravery that people can only hope to achieve in their lifetimes. Don’t buy this book if you’re looking for tepid, feel-good reading, but do buy it if you want gentle humor and beautiful descriptions of love and tenderness from an unexpectedly feisty little family. I promise that sorrow is tempered with joy and the book is well worth a read. It gets all the stars from me!

instruction: I'm an American going to France for the first time, and I know a little French I learned in school, but I'm afraid to speak it because I've heard that if you don't speak it perfectly, that people won't want to talk to you or help you with directions or information you might need. At the same time, I watched "Emily in Paris" and they weren't very happy about her not even trying to speak English... so what do I do?
reference: Au contraire, mon ami - any little bit of French you might speak will be very appreciated! Never mind poor Emily - she is far from a realistic character, and as for the French people in the series, their French cultural traits are somewhat exaggerated. As for Paris, think of it the same way as you would any large city - New York, for example. People are in a hurry, living their lives, rushing from work to appointments to pick up their children from school, etc., and they may not have a lot of time to talk to you. And if you have a sense of humor and don't take yourself too seriously, the whole country will teach you French. Allow people to correct you, and don't worry if they don't act extremely enthusiastic about your presence - French people can be more reserved in the North. If you go down South, you may find people somewhat more gregarious. If you want to blend in a bit, dress somewhat conservatively and wear comfortable shoes. If you end up not liking the clothes or shoes you are wearing, you can always do a little shopping, American Express is an international language. ;) Bon voyage!

instruction: Write a funny tale about a terrible employee at a burger restaurant who gets caught slacking on the job and is delivered justice. Include notes of disgust in your writing, and make sure the employee (Clay) is unlikable.
reference: “What are you, the health inspector?” laughed Clay while brushing past the stranger who was giving him a dirty look. The disdain came from the fact the stranger, who indeed was the regional health inspector, determined there was no possibility Clay could have washed his hands between the brief moment when the toilet flushed and the doorknob turned. Clay was a cook at a small burger restaurant. For the most part, Clay was a decent worker, except he had a loud mouth and a short temper. An additional character flaw of Clay’s was not having the greatest sense of awareness about him. Maintaining this, he never saw his coworkers attempting to gain his attention via flailing arms. If he had given them his attention, they surely would have made certain Clay knew who he was talking to and, possibly, might have kept him from making any further mistakes. Since the attempt had failed, Clay continued his normal behavior. He returned to his grill station and produced his spatula from his rear pocket. The health inspector never saw him pick up any utensils, so Clay must have taken the spatula into the bathroom with him. Purely disgusted, the health inspector walked over to Clay’s station to continue his assessment. “If you want a burger,” Clay rolled his eyes and turned away, “you are going to have to put an order in up front. However, when you do that, make sure they tell me who it is for so I can prepare it special, just for you.” The health inspector, assuming Clay’s special burger was nothing anyone would want to consume, realized Clay was not fit to serve food to the public. Finally, the stranger pulled his wallet from a coat pocket and revealed his credentials. Clay could not believe it. In shock, his mouth stayed open long enough for a thin stream of drool to fall from his mouth and land on the cooktop. “I will be sure to include this in the report, too.” grinned the health inspector.
