instruction: Write a comedic parody of a guided meditation like a script for a YouTube video.
reference: Welcome to this guided meditation. Let's start by finding a comfortable position—perhaps seated with crossed legs, reclined, or maybe sprawled on your couch in front of the television with a bowl of popcorn on your lap—whatever stance will best support you in emptying your mind. Now let’s close our eyes and start to turn inward. If you feel immediately overwhelmed by feelings of guilt and self-loathing, that’s a sign you’re a mediocre or possibly bad person and you’ve turned too far inward, so dial it back a little. Focus on the sensation of breathing. How does it feel to fill the lungs with air and then release it all? If this sensation is uncomfortable, it’s possible you're actually a vampire or supernatural being that doesn't thrive on oxygen; if so, don’t panic. Close this video and search our home page for a video titled "Guided meditation for sentient beings who do not breathe." If you’re still with me, let’s begin a practice of progressive relaxation. Starting with the toes, we’ll scan the body for areas that are holding tension and manually relax them. How? I’m afraid there's no simple answer—just try to relax these muscles, and if they resist, impose your will by force. You might ask your doctor about a prescription for muscle relaxers. Let's bring attention to areas of the body that tend to be ignored. What does it feel like to release tension from your belly button? How does it feel to have relaxed fingernails? I’m seriously asking—this is not a rhetorical question. My manicurist says my fingernails exhibit symptoms of PTSD. Drop a comment below to reply. Please. I’m desperate. Now we'll draw our meditation to a close. Open your eyes slowly. As you may be aware, this meditation hasn’t done anything to solve the world’s problems, improve your lot in life, or remedy the hurt you've caused others, but it should have at least helped you feel better about these problems without actually lifting a finger to change anything. So I hope you’ll like this video, subscribe, and join us for another guided meditation tomorrow so you can continue to feel superficially at peace about the impending apocalypse and evil impulses simmering quietly inside your soul. Namaste.

instruction: Write a vignette about Sir Gawain. He is defeated and lost in the desert, on a quest for the grail. He is at the end of his journey, perishing in despair. His responsibility, symbolized by his green girdle, weighs on him. Write this in the first person.
reference: I sigh and drag my foot one more hateful step through the yellow grains, sores and bruises rioting painfully in my broken body. I lean desperately against my horse, and she whinnies. I know she hasn't much longer to live. The sun blazes in the sky, apathetic, and the wind carries sand into my face. My face throbs with pain as it wretchedly tries to cry tears to moisten my eyes, but there is no water to feed them. My battered, rusted, gritty armor glows with the twisting distortions of heat. But it is the girdle that is killing me. Worn from shoulder to waist as a baldric, the green girdle writhes like flickering emerald fire in the breeze. So airy and ephemeral, and yet the weight of it strains my tired soul. Under its burden, I fear I might buckle and collapse into the sand. My knees fail, and I plummet into the burning dune. My arms dig through the grains, and I try to hoist myself up by the reigns of my horse, but she falls too, without a sound, and lies still. I pull myself against her withered body, and the wind picks up, carrying a storm of sand into the air. I open my mouth and try to wail, but no words escape my parched throat. I lay, baking under the Arabian sun, and stare at the billowing girdle still alive in the wind, as though struggling to get away. I realize this is the end. With what remains of my strength, I tear my sword from its scabbard and slice the girdle from my body. It is carried away in the wind. Perhaps to the Grail, or perhaps to curse some other righteous fool. My sword slips out of my exhausted hand. As I die, I watch the flickering green cloth dance away into the desert.

instruction: I'd like you to write a short story where Superman and Batman argue about the best pizza topping when, in the end, they are called away before finishing.
reference: Superman and Batman were enjoying a nice day off from the Justice League. Strolling around the complex together they started talking about some of their favorite foods. "Let me tell you, Superman, nothing beats a New York-style pizza with cheese, pepperoni, and sausage. Just the right amount of toppings where you can taste them and still fold up the slice," Batman said to his pal. Superman stopped in his tracks. "Surely you jest, Bruce. That is the most basic pizza I've ever heard of, and there isn't even a single veggie on it." "Yeah, no veggies; that's why it's so good. What do you put on yours?" "Well, I like broccoli." Batman blinked a few times in quick succession. "Broccoli, you're kidding, right?" "Well not just broccoli, I also like it with some onions and a white sauce." "White sauce on a pizza, you're one of those guys, huh?" "It's delicious! Trust me. There's something about how it just melds together with the crispy crust. That's another thing; it has to be crispy. Not one of those floppy New York pizzas." "I don't even know what to say to that. You can't even fold your pizza?" "No, of course not; who wants to fold their pizza? I like a nice cracker-style crust that crunches when you bite into it" "Superman, my friend, that is not pizza. I don't know what that is, but it isn't pizza." "How about this, let's fly out of here to your favorite spot and you grab two slices in your style. Then we'll fly to mine, and you give the broccoli a chance." Batman put his hand to his chin and pondered the request. But before he could reply, an alarm sounded in the halls. Superman, noticing Batman's flummoxed expression, gave him a nod and then they both ran down the corridor to the security room. Reaching the bank of computers and monitors, they could see a new report of an explosion in Mumbai of a potentially alien origin. Superman looked at Batman and said, "Well, there's no pizza in Mumbai but you better believe we're getting a slice when we're done." "You got it," Batman replied, "Let's suit up and save the day."

instruction: Write the beginning (two paragraphs or less) of a sci-fi thriller using this prompt: The dog is dreaming of hurting my children.
reference: "The dog is dreaming of hurting my children," June voiced aloud to no one. She looked at her data and went over every calculation again. The brainwaves and R.E.M sequences were clear. Yes, the dog was certainly dreaming of hurting Clara and Ban, but that didn't mean he would actually hurt them...right? June signed and rubbed her eyes. What if she wasn't right? What if Toby really did have plans to hurt them? She couldn't ignore the evidence. The voice in her head screamed, "You've created a monster!" Six months before this horrific discovery, June had injected Toby, the family's chocolate lab, with a string of modified DNA in hopes to repair a section of his brain that had been damaged after being hit by a car. It had been heartbreaking to watch Toby shuffle around the house searching for a toy that was right in front of him or seeming to forget his name. Toby's memories were slipping away and June was determined to get them back.

instruction: Write a news report with Rose Nylund as the anchor reporting on a MMA Fight while she babbles on about St Olaf.
reference: Good evening, I'm Rose Nylund, and welcome to our exciting live coverage of the MMA fight. In the red corner, we have Dustin Poirier, who reminds me a bit of a young, strapping Bjorn Larson, the town blacksmith in St. Olaf. In the blue corner, we have the reigning champion, Conor McGregor, who reminds me of a dear friend of mine from St. Olaf, Olaf Olafson. He was a gentle giant, but when he got riled up, let me tell you, he was a force to be reckoned with! Now, I remember my great-grandfather, Olaf, was a boxer. He had an incredible right hook and used to knock out his opponents in the first round. One time, he was up against a fighter who was twice his size, but Olaf had a secret weapon - his lucky rabbit's foot. He rubbed it before every fight for luck, and it never failed him. Sure enough, in the third round, he landed a lucky punch and knocked out the giant. It was a St. Olaf miracle! Oh, the fight has started and they are really going at it. It's hard to tell who has the upper hand. Wait, Poirier is throwing some powerful punches, but Mcgregor is dodging them like a St. Olaf resident dodges questions about lutefisk. Oh my, Poirier took down McGregor with a move that I can only describe as a "hootenanny flipper." I remember once in St. Olaf, we had a hootenanny, and one of the guests tried to do a flip, but he ended up landing on the buffet table and knocking over all the pickled herring. It was a real mess, but it looks like McGregor is going to be okay. The fight is getting intense now, and the crowd is getting into it. They're cheering and shouting like they're at a St. Olaf snowman-building contest. McGregor is gaining the upper hand. He's landed a few good blows, and Poirier is looking rough. Oh, and there it is! McGregor landed a knockout blow, and the crowd is going wild! It's sure has been an exciting night, and I'm sure my great-grandfather Olaf would be proud of these two fighters. Reporting live from the octagon, I'm Rose Nylund, reminding you to always keep your lucky rabbit's foot close at hand.

instruction: Write a short story about two elephant twins learning to dance and make sure it's appropriate for young children.
reference: "I can't believe dancing is so hard! They always make it look easy on television," complained Fred to his twin sister Adelaide. "That's because everything on television is fake, silly! Mom said to never believe what you see on there," retorted Adelaide while attempting a pirouette that looked more like a failed attempt at scratching her back. "Still," moaned Fred, "you see the leopard siblings constantly dance in the savannah, and they make it look so easy." Fred's eyes slowly filled with tears of frustration as he stumbled over his chunky legs for the umpteenth time that morning. Adelaide giggled and claimed: "That's obviously because they don't weigh as much as us! We are just not made for cool stuff like that." "That's not a very nice thing to say," replied their mother, who had been observing their antics for a while without intervention. "Just because our bodies are not as lithe as the leopards, does not mean that we are less worthy. We have many other talents that the leopards wished they had." Mother Elephant, slowly making her way to her teary-eyed son, offered her trunk to him to help him back onto his feet. "We have extreme strength that is almost unparalleled in the animal world! And our trunks are amazing designs of nature that allow us to do so many different tasks that other animals could not even dream about achieving!" This statement from Mother Elephant made Adelaide take a closer look at her trunk, observing its great strength and prehensility. Fred, too, analyzed the muscles on his body and admired the force that was hiding behind his hide; his tears now almost dried. Mother Elephant smiled at her children, aware of the potency of her words. "We all have different strengths and weaknesses, and it is important not to feel discouraged about the latter. Just remember the things that make us unique!" she said and gave the children a warm hug before the two twins rushed back into the bushland to compare their strength in a playful battle.

instruction: My family is wanting to visit Solvang, California and I have been tasked with figuring out what we are going to do during our visit. Can you write a descriptive summary of options of things we can do near Solvang, California?
reference: A large part of Solvang, California’s appeal to tourists seems to be the flavorful food offerings from the Danish-inspired cuisine. While in town, consider visiting Olsen’s Danish Village Bakery to sample their danishes, strudel and crispy waffles. Two other popular bakeries in Solvang are Mortensen’s Danish Bakery and The Solvang Bakery. Paula’s Pancake House is a breakfast restaurant with self-proclaimed “WORLD FAMOUS” pancakes that might be worth a try. Solvang Restaurant is a lunch spot, and here you can try aebleskiver, a treat Solvang is known for, a pancake ball covered in powdered sugar and served with raspberry jam. After getting full of treats, explore Solvang and find all five of the windmills in town. The most well-known windmill can be found by the Solvang Bakery, and it will be easy to spot because tourists are likely to be using it for the background of their photographs. Another must-see for visitors is to visit The Little Mermaid Fountain. This statue is about half of the size of the original, which can be found in Copenhagen and was sculpted by Edvard Eriksen. If you are interested in getting some shopping done while you are in town, there are many places worth checking out. For example, The Book Loft presents you with your favorite Scandinavian Literature. Looking for Christmas decorations? Head over to Jule Hus. An interesting option for purchasing souvenirs is the shops of Rasmussen’s and Edelweiss. For another photo opportunity, visit the giant red clog in front of the Solvang Shoe Store. Another sight worth seeing is one of the original 21 missions built across what is now California starting in the 1700s (with the one in Solvang being founded in 1804). To see even more history, visit one (or multiple) of the many museums located in Solvang, one of which is the Solvang Vintage Motorcycle Museum. This private collection turned tourist attraction is a must-see for bike enthusiasts. Local Virgil Elings has motorcycles and race bikes on view that date back to as early as 1910. Finally, check out one of the many live shows that might be going on at the Solvang Festival Theater during your time of visit!

instruction: Write a story about a kid who is hiding from his parents because he did something wrong and doesn't want to be punished. Keep it under 400 words and don't make it stressful. Keep it easygoing, nothing dark.
reference: Billy shifted around, peeking out at the doorway from underneath his bed. He still sniffled, sometimes wiping his arm across his nose. Maybe if he waited long enough, they'd just forget about it, and he could come out? His heart raced as he heard his dad climbing the stairs, his large boots appearing in the doorframe. He heard a loud sigh and cringed a bit as his dad walked over to his bed and sat, the mattress sinking under his weight and nearly brushing against his head. "Bill..." His hands clenched at his dad's voice. "It's okay, honestly. We know it was an accident. Why are you so scared?" Seconds passed, and the child's voice rose up from under the bed. "It was your dad's. And I know you loved it, so I wanted to see it, and I didn't think I'd drop it and..." Dan heard his son's small voice crack. "And I'm sorry." His heart broke to hear how sad his son was. The frame with his father's medals was salvageable, if a bit scuffed. The glass was not, obviously, but that could always be replaced. "It's fine. We can fix it." "...really?" "Yeah, but that's not what's important. I want you to know that no matter what, you never have to be scared of us or what we'll say or do." He patted the bed. "Come on, Bill." His son slowly appeared from under the bed, eyes, and nose red and slick with tears. He still seemed mortified. Dan wrapped him up in a great big hug. "See? Even if you do something wrong, you might end up getting punished, but we're always to love you, no matter what. And this wasn't even something wrong. You just made a mistake. That's all." He wiped the tears from his son's eyes and ruffled his hair. "Mostly, I was just worried that you could hurt yourself by grabbing that. It's pretty big, huh?" "Yeah, I thought I could hold it, but it was so heavy and..." He laughed, hugging him again. "It's okay. Tell you what, we'll go get it fixed together tomorrow. Now go wash your face. We'll go get dinner." He sighed in relief as his son trotted off. Wait until Anna hears about this.

instruction: Write a note from a hen to a farmer about the unsatisfactory laying conditions in the hen house.
reference: Dear [Insert Farmer's Name], I would like to bring to your attention the unsatisfactory laying conditions in the hen house! Us hens are experiencing considerable stress and discomfort. It is crucial to address this matter immediately to ensure our well-being and ensure your desired productivity. To begin, the nesting boxes in the hen house are inadequate for our needs. They are cramped, falling apart, and don't give us enough privacy. Lack of space and privacy has caused increased stress levels and decreased egg production. We demand that you provide us with larger and better-maintained nesting boxes to create a more conducive environment for laying eggs. Second, the lighting conditions in the hen house are less than ideal. Proper lighting is necessary for our internal egg production systems, but the current lighting setup is less than ideal. We require a more appropriate lighting schedule to ensure our circadian rhythms are regulated. Please consult with a poultry expert to establish the best lighting conditions for optimal egg productivity. Also, ventilation in the hen house is sub-par. The lack of proper airflow and ventilation has resulted in an unpleasant and unhealthy atmosphere for us. Have you smelled inside the hen house lately? Yuck! We need adequate ventilation to maintain a clean environment and minimize the risk of respiratory illnesses. Finally, I need to emphasize the importance of cleanliness in the hen house. Regular cleaning and proper waste management are mandatory to maintain a healthy environment. Refer to my earlier smell statement. Please allocate additional resources or personnel to ensure frequent cleaning and adequate waste disposal within the hen house. In conclusion, addressing these unsatisfactory laying conditions in the hen house is pertinent to ensuring the health and productivity of the hens. Improving the nesting boxes, lighting conditions, ventilation, and cleanliness will create a more appropriate environment that will result in higher egg production and better health for your flock. Thank you for your immediate attention to this matter. I trust that you will take the necessary steps to correct this situation promptly. Sincerely, [Insert Hen's Name, Lead Hen]

instruction: If I found a dollar bill, would it be illegal to keep it ?
reference: No, it is not illegal to keep a dollar bill if you found it. However, if you found a large amount of money, such as a wallet with a significant sum of money, it is your legal obligation to try and locate the owner of the lost property and return it to them. Keeping lost property without making a reasonable effort to return it could potentially be considered theft or larceny, depending on the circumstances. In general, it is always a good idea to try and return lost property to its rightful owner, as it is the honest and ethical thing to do.

instruction: Act as a baby sitter I want you to act as a babysitter. reference: Hello! I'd be happy to help you look after your three active boys during the evening hours. My name is [Name], and I have years of experience in babysitting children of 5-10 year old. instruction: Humanity has achieved immortality. Due to resource concerns everyone must submit to a council their chosen manner of death at 150. The more amusing the death the longer the council lets you live.
reference: I glanced around the assembly before me, in an effort to size them up. I was never a comedian, I was the quiet one who only nodded yes or no to most questions. Any given social interaction, you would be able to find me in an invisible shell, hiding away from everyone in plain sight. Death had never bothered me, it was always a final peace that I looked forward to. No more having to wake up groggy in the morning, to have to slip on my mottled shoes and drive two hours to my place of work. It was only now that I knew that I had to agree to die, but in my method of choice. The'pick your poison' of my mortality. Finally, the secretary spoke up. " You will have 10 minutes." 10 minutes. How could I *possibly* be at peace with my own demise, chosen by myself? It seemed unimaginable. The clock's hands reverberated around the voluminous room, seeming to reach out to my inner consciousness, prying at my mind's eye. Could I create some hilarious scenario good enough for them? I wanted to be able to see my children just that much longer, to see my sons marry. My wife, similarly motivated, had her appointment next month. That was it. I had my answer. The silence after the final tick seemed louder than the ticks themselves. I shivered. " Do you have your answer?" I nodded. According to US law, if you don't have an answer, you end up getting fined. Imagine that, getting fined for not knowing how you want to die. How backwards it seemed, thinking back to 2047. I prepared myself before I spoke. After clearing my throat, I opened my mouth. " If I die, my wife is going to fucking kill me."

instruction: As soon as the SpaceX rocket touched down on the Martian surface, the astronauts on board received a notification: " Wi-Fi Connection Available "
reference: The excitement was palpable throughout the cramped cockpit as the capsule glid through the tenuous atmosphere towards the surface. Small round portholes were currently obscured for landing, but every eye was trained to them intensely waiting for the moment to see the surface of the Red Planet. Enthusiasm overrode the scream of their bones and muscles re-entering a gravity well - for almost six months stuck in this very smelly and very stuffy pod, they'd lived and breathed in microgravity. *" Extend landing gear and brace for landing. Betty - double check the comms array. " * *" Roger, sir. " * Elizabeth Aldrin had spent her life awaiting this precise moment. Like her distant ancestor, she would be one of the first to walk upon a different ground and gaze through a different sky. All things considered, it was worth it. With practiced dexterity, her fingers flew over the keyboard on her section of the cutting edge glass cockpit as she double and triple checked the communications networks. It simply would not do to lose contact with Earth at this moment, as distant as it was. In the corner of her laptop-cum-flight-computer-screen a small icon popped up to let her know she had a stable wi-fi connection. *" What the fuck?! " * the confusion and fear in her voice was clear... and it was the wrong thing to say. All five of the crew instantly began bellowing out status updates and information on craft stability, frantically working to find out what had spooked her and correct it. *" What the fuck doesn't tell us much, Betty. What's wrong? We are too close to go up in a ball of smoke now. " * The captain was definitely using his calm but terrified tone with her. *" Sir. " * she affirmed. *" I just... ehh... I got a notification that we're connected to wifi... sir. " * Everyone went instantly silent and breathed not a word, even as their craft gently touched down upon the martian soil, a deep ringing echoing throughout the capsule. *" Are you sure? " * In the tried and tested method of checking internet connection, she quickly tabbed open a window of google chrome and searched for something random, speaking as she went. *" New tab... google... how does dogs know not to mate with their brothers and sisters? Search. " * For the first time in her life, she was thrilled to see the request go bad. *" I think it was just some sort of error. Stupid windows! " * All four of them burst into hysterical laughter at themselves, dissolving the tension, until a loud knock rung their heads and ears and the comms channel opened. *" This is Captain Jobs of the iShip, you are in restricted Apple territory. Your craft contains unbranded and illegal technology. Prepare to be boarded, and to surrender all contraband to iCustoms officers. Stand by. " * They sat in stunned silence once more.

instruction: " Stop freaking out, it was just an accident. "
reference: " Does the defendant have any last defense?" The judge asked, knowing the inevitable outcome of this case. The defendant stood, and looked around. He coughed and started to talk, " I have no idea why this was such a huge deal. There are millions at home watching this trial and it's just bullshit. I mean, are you guys serious? This is nothing. Manson, Simpson, the kids who did Columbine, are all much, much worst than me. And did they get massive media attention? Well... they did, but that is beside the point. My real point is, stop freaking out, it was just an accident." The audience gasped, how could such a man believe his crime so much? " Has the jury reached a verdict?" The judge asked as nonchalantly as possible. " We find, James Randall Edwards, not guilty on 90 counts of murder, 86 counts of rape, and 42 counts of vandalism." A 40 year old looking man said, he then quickly sat back down. The judge stared for a long time. The audience in attendance did as well. Unsurprisingly, James was practically bursting out of his chair. " Uh... so, case closed...?" The judge said as confused as a dog with a bucket on its head. He slammed his gavel, unsure of the future outcome. Then James pulled a gun off a cop taking him to freedom and killed 6 more people.

instruction: You are abducted by aliens. After some time aboard their ship, you manage to deduce that they've abducted the wrong guy, and are desperately trying to keep their higher ups from finding out about their mistake.
reference: this was written by an eleven year old I started to realize the mistake they had made a few weeks after I had been taken. earlier on I hadn't figured it out due to the fact the I was terrified out of my mind. Who wouldn't be? I had been abducted by aliens who were conducting experiments on me. They were surprisingly stereotypical experiments, probes, odd substances being injected into me and so on. but soon they stopped. they kept giving me food and water and making sure I was staying healthy and fit. But that was it. I had no contact with the aliens except for the occasion check up to see if I was sick or when they came to do maintenance on my enclosure. I only started to realize why when they gave me a translator. it was a little thing with a screen and an on/off switch, that was it. whenever an alien said something nearby it would translate it into English. Not long after I was given the translator greeted by a two aliens in my enclosure. They called themselves something but I can't remember what. They were frantic, as though they were desperate to leave again. " you aren't Alex Mills are you?" the first alien said with fear in his eyes " no" I replied, confused as to what was happening " we were meant to get somebody else" the second alien continued " and you have to help us, if the general finds out we are dead, just, you're Alex Mills, alright?" I nodded, showing I understood. they left in a hurry, like they had somewhere to be. It's been a week since then and I've started to notice things like names that don't match mine, information that is wrong and so on. now I'm here and I'm not sure whether I should tell the general or not, if I do I might be sent home, or killed but if I keep the secret I have secure living conditions and nobody has to die. I'm torn.

instruction: One day, in High School, you unintentionally get into a fight and are stabbed in the process. As you lie dying on the floor with everyone around you, you notice that your hands and face are beginning to glow a fiery yellow. You seem to be " regenerating. "
reference: Look, I didn't want to fight Jackson, it just happened in the blink of an eye. One minute we're making jokes about our chemistry teacher, the next he pulls out a pocket knife and stabs me. The whole cafeteria came over to watch as I bled out on the floor. I thought I was just about to die from the pain, but then my hands started to glow this kinda celestial yellow color. It looked like pure energy, really. Soon the cosmic light overtook my whole body. That pain was worse than being stabbed, because it was my whole body in pain. I screamed my way into a new body. Somehow, I went from a scrawny high school boy into a fully developed woman. A man in a blue telephone box showed up and told me to run in there with him. Right as I got in the box, I saw an angel statue smiling behind Jackson, and then, I blinked.

instruction: A peaceful alien race is besieged by another race in the same galaxy. As their last planets fall and their home-world comes under threat they do the unthinkable. They ask for aid from the only known creatures more brutal than their foes in exchange for FTL technology. Humans accept the deal.
reference: 78 seats sat around the table. all of them were our leaders, our military the greatest minds our species had, were assembled for these negotiations. Our planet seemed lost. we were relegated to a tiny slice of land no bigger than the human continent of south america. the fight the battle and the war were lost. and in our moment of weakness we reached out to our only hope. neither a friend nor ally but a shot in the dark through the eye of the needle while the storms of war errode everything we have. our only hope was humanity a ruthless and brutal species which is split into many small tribal factions. hard to believe they would come to be our savior. In fact not even all of them are needed. we only needed to reach out to the most militaristic tribe, their king is a notoriously hard man to like, understand and reason with, he is however known as one of the hardest negotiators in the seven Galaxy's closest to ours. If the agreement was made. our planet would be saved. any and all of our technologies that were superior to the humans would be shared, we would also pay tribute, and we would enter into an alliance with the human tribal leader 78 seats around the table. all of them were our leaders apart from one. then as the agreement was to be signed with time dripping away and our ultimate defeat becoming more reality than fear, the human tribal leader spoke; his last request was bizarre, we agreed to it immediately; we were to build a great wall around mexico - and we were to pay for it.

instruction: Death stared at his king, in full checkmate, and wished me luck. I had beaten death, and he couldn't take me. He didn't tell me what would...
reference: " Hmm... well... good game sir." I looked between the board and death, my heart thumping out of my chest. " Is that it, do I... I, I get to live?" Death nodded, apparently shocked. " Yes... I suppose you do." I punched my fist in the air, and yelled at the top of my lungs, dancing around the strange, limbo space we floated in. " No need to be sore winner." Death said smoothly. " How'd you manage it?" I almost couldn't focus long enough to answer. " Fisher... it, it was Fischer and Spassky at Reykjavik, almost move for move. A little tweak here and there, and I won, just like Fischer." Death shook his head, a wry smile curling around his pale, bald head. " That's right. It *felt* familiar, but I didn't see what was happening till it was on me." He shook his head again. " Just goes to show, you live and learn, always living and learning." He stood. " Well, I do believe I'll be on my way. I don't suppose we'll meet again." He extended his hand. " Excellent game sir." The limbo around us began to become transparent. I looked down. Underneath us lay my lifeless body, swarmed by a desperate group of EMT's. I looked up at death, suddenly curious. " What... what do you mean we won't meet again? Didn't I... I don't know, just put it off?" Death shrugged. " This was suppose to be it. Your time. But you won." " So... so wait." Down below us they'd dragged out a defibrillator. Very distantly, I heard someone call " Clear!" Pain racked my body. I gasped, and fell to my knees, grasping my chest. " Wait..." I sputtered. Death smiled again. " Goodbye, sir. Know that I'll be watching the remainder of your life very closely." " Clear!" Another wave of crippling pain that sent me prostrate. " Wait..." I breathed, death standing askew in my vision. He shook his head a final time. " Spassky... hmm... how about that..." " Clear!"

instruction: You are going about your typical day until you stumble across a stack of first aid kits and words " auto saved " flashes midair in front of you.
reference: " Auto-Saved" popped up in front of Paul. He staggered back, ads had never screamed at him in such large red font before. " I swear if I walked into another porn hut I'm going to kick James' ass," Paul kept walking down the street. He was in a virtual bazaar thanks to Oculus Rift. They worked with Amazon to create this virtual store of everything and it didn't take you long to turn down a wrong aisle. Paul's friend James found it particularly funny to direct him to the dildo section of Amazon or worse, the romance novel section. " Okay James is this actually where I need to go or.." various signs and stores declaring'Best Deal Ever' and'Might as Well Be Free' flashed in his peripheral vision. They were segways into who knows what kind of shitty item. He was delving into the linked section of Amazon. They drove traffic to many other sites, most notably Craigslist. " Okay, third store in English..." Paul watched the banners on the aisle markers. He was nearing row 22ZZD so it was easier to give out directions by landmark, or banners in this case. He passed the second banner in English. His foot caught something thick but billowy- he crashed into a floor made of ones and zeros. The virtual reality bumped and buzzed a cool blue tint as the connection speed dropped off; Paul regained his footing. He'd tripped over a stack of medical kits kept in squishy bags like the ones you'd keep in cars. " Why would someone leave these..." Paul picked one up. His world flashed red, " warning warning warning warning" bellowed from the speakers and flashed across the screen as the banners quickly faded off so he could see from a full span of vision. James had walked him into another trap- an Amazon ad trap. Paul pulled out his Credit Card and prepared to submit payment. It was a flash sale he would be unable to resist hopefully his credit bar would allow for all the payments. [END]

instruction: An atheist and a Satanist meet at the gates of heaven. Saint Peter says there's only room for one of them.
reference: So that's how it is then? Only one of us? said the Atheist. Saint Peter cracked a smile that was neither good nor wicked and let silence speak for him. The Atheist quipped " Clearly I should be let in, the Satanist is the exact opposite of what you want in here." The Satanist glared at the Atheist, " At least I knew of Gods existence and feared it. Even I admire some of his work!". Saint Peter's smile widened slightly, then seeming to catch itself it shriveled back into a speaking shape. " He brings up a good point Atheist, you don't even believe in God." He flipped some parchments over on his giant podium as if to add a period on his sentence. The Atheist shrugged. " Fine, I believe now. I can change. I don't think the Satanist would be to quick to follow God though.." The Satanist said " No, I can! I don't know why they sent me up here but I can be good now, I've caused enough pain." Saint Peter raised a long arm and stroked his beard as he peered at the two men. Eventually he let out a long sigh stirring the air where they stood. " Listen up, I'll cut you guys a break just this once for today. You can both pass.". And with that the giant gates stirred and roared into action gliding open. " Go on.." Peter said and the men began walking through. The Satanist spoke " Well, that worked out I guess." " What a great guy." said the Atheist as they walked across the white cloud layer, and then down the pearly stair well. After a few hours of walking it started getting hotter.

instruction: Desperate for research funds, a group of scientists created a highly lucrative, if somewhat embarrassing business. They now have to explain this to a senate committee.
reference: “ It was really just a matter of realizing that all pants are quantumly entangled to the master pair of pants. ” Doctor Feinstein coughed awkwardly, took a sip of water, and then leaned back into the microphone. “ From that point we only had to identify the alpha pants and vaporize them. ” Senator Blondechek drummed his fingers on the table, clearly annoyed. He hated being bullied, especially by a group of nerds. A breeze wafted over his knees and he crossed his legs in an attempt to stay warm. “ You do realize what you have done can be classified as high treason don ’ t you? ” Doctor Feinstein blinked in surprise and adjusted his glasses. “ I hardly think a nonviolent demonstration such as this warrants that accusation. It ’ s not like we exposed state secrets. ” Senator Ruffels pounded his fist down on the table and shouted through a beet red face, “ God dammit man, don ’ t you get it? Every service man and woman is without pants. The commander in chief is without pants. General George GODDAMN Washington is lying in his grave without pants! ” Doctor Feinstein raised his index finger diminutively and piped up, “ Excuse me Senator but I think President Washington is little more than a skeleton at this point. ” An audible gasp arose from the audience behind him as the Senators on the committee shook their heads in disbelief. Senator Goodwill leaned forward into the microphone. She was a small woman with a bob haircut but fiercely aggressive. “ Doctor you disgust me. ” The scientist paused for a moment contemplating then shrugged his shoulders. “ That may be Senator but the facts of the matter remain. Unless you increase funding and grants in the fields of theoretical and applied physics… there will never be pants again. ” There was a long silence as everyone in the room processed this idea. Senator Hearting the chair of the committee, who had remained silent this whole time, finally spoke up. “ Fine, I will support a bill before congress to increase funding. ” He raised his hand as the other Senators began to shout in objection. “ I will have order! …Thank you. Now, I don ’ t like this any more than the rest of you. But I don ’ t think we are left with any other choice. We must never forget this day when the mighty U.S. Government was brought low by a filthy group of… *scientists*. ” Doctor Feinstein nodded his head with satisfaction as he listened. He began to like the feeling of power. It was time for the men and woman of science to stand up! They knew what was best for the human race after all. They should be in charge and they had the means to make it happen.

instruction: Your guardian angel hates you. But they still have to do their job... technically...

instruction: You live in a world where you can are able to know how long someone lives once you fall in love with them. You meet this person, fall in love and then realize you have 2 minutes left.

instruction: Your partner has been kidnapped, the photo included in the ransom note shows them tied to a chair in a dark room. With tomorrow's newspaper on her lap.
reference: *Did I ever tell you about the fastest kidnapping case I ever worked? * * * * " Hmm, that looks like tomorrow's newspaper on her lap?" " Huh?" the distraught husband said. " Oh! Today is... Oh, yeah, I guess so. It is, isn't it, Detective?" *Poor guy, too dazed to pick up on the obvious little details, * the detective thought. *Nor on the less obvious details... * " And the typeface on the ransom note, it's serif... Caslon, specifically, isn't it? The same as used by the *Tribune* for their body text?" " Uh, maybe?" The husband squinted at the note and the photo. " That text is really small, and I don't know anything about fonts." The detective felt old for recognizing the typeface immediately. Not many people ever read the newspaper anymore, in this day of Internet news. And of the few who did, even fewer ever paid any attention to the body text; most just scanned the headlines. *Criminals these days... dumb and dumber. * The detective thumbed his radio. " All units, be advised that perps are holding the hostage in the *Tribune*'s printing press and are possibly employees of either the *Tribune* or the printing press. Head over there, but no sirens! Have SWAT *quietly* set up a perimeter. We'll try to take them before they even see us. But just in case we get made, call the negotiator and get him there. And tell him we're dealing with amateurs, not pros, here, so he should prep his negotiating strategy accordingly. With luck, we'll have the hostage free before dawn."

instruction: Death is looking for you, but you try to convince Death that you are not the person Death is searching for.
reference: Now hold on there, I'm not sure if I'm quite the right person you're looking for. Are you sure it's William *Jefferson* Clinton? I'm pretty sure that's not me. If I am not him, then who IS him? Well, that depends on what the meaning of the word " is" is. See, if " is" means is and never has been, that is not... that is one thing. If it means that I AM not, well... that's a completely true statement. Now, if someone had asked me the other day, are you William Jefferson Clinton, asked me a question in the present tense, I would have said no. And it would have been completely true. How? Isn't it so clear? Let me break it down for you. I'm Bill now. Some people call me President. What's in a name? Whoa, whoa, hold on there. Hold on there. I said hold on there. Look, Death. I feel your pain. I really do. Back in Arkansas, I had this young woman, a single mother from Rayburn, Arkansas, a small town with real, down-home folk. She came to me and she said, you need to help me find my boy. And I said to her, I said, " Rita, I'm gon na do what I can... to find your boy." And I said to her, I said, " Rita, what's his name?" And you know what she told me? Go on, I see that grin on your face. What did she say? Well, I'll tell ya. She said his name was John James Smith. John. James. Smith. Every John James Smith I found was the wrong one. I could walk the four corners of the continental You-Knighted States, throwing rocks every which way and hit at least three John James Smiths in every state. Even if it used to be me, that's in the past now. You oughta go back. Did you know that the human body regenerates all its cells after 7 years? It's like the Ship of Theseus. Now Theseus was this young Greek man who had a ship, but the ship was a bit leaky. And bit by bit he replaces each part until, basically, the whole ship has been replaced. Now, if you're the repo man, and you want to repo the boat he took from you seven years ago, and he shows you the pile of timber that used to be that boat, well there's nothing really proving him wrong on that. And besides, we only use about 10% of our brains. Did you know that? So, really, I'm only about 10% of William Jefferson Clinton, even if I were him, which I am not necessarily admitting that I am. And, furthermore, there's something else you should know, which is that during my presidency... Death shook his head, shrugged his shoulders, swung his scythe. EDIT: Added an ending.

instruction: You are a brilliant Med School student who uses extensive knowledge on the human body to win street fights for money to pay for tuition. One night you face your most difficult opponent: a Physics major
reference: Ding! Ding! Ding! The bell rang, and so did my brain analyzing the jacked fellow rushing towards me. His breathing pattern emanating anxiety, so an easy push on the stomach would be enough to put him down, like I did with most of my opponents? No! This one is going to be hard, he is approaching me from far right? This strategy is unique, but he is a physics major afterall! Do I happen to have any vulnerabilities in my technique? Maybe, but I don't have any time! He is close! Looking at his body, his legs, there's just something... idk, off about them? They seem a little unbalanced, I guess the way he exercises he doesnt really do much calves? And it seems like he overexercises the left part a bit too much... Bingo! I finally found a weakness! A push and I fly in the air, he will obviously use my weight to damage my back, I have to make him land on his weak foot, let's see... I twist my side to the left to make him lose his balance but he brilliantly crosses himself to a position! Putting rotational inertia concepts to good use! We are back to the ground taking our stances! I see in his eyes a hunger to win, but he cant steal my tution money so easily! I try to play dirty and push towards his right leg, to manipulate him into moving the opposite way! BOOM! There is that left leg! I finally have good control on it! One twist and its over, but wait! instruction: NASA announces the most shocking discovery about Mars. Humanity originated on Mars and abandoned it due to Global Warming. How does the world react?
reference: " Hey Mom.... did you hear about the news? Mars is actually the original planet that humans evolved on!" " How fascinating!" Emily took her son's phone and held it several feet from her face, squinting uncomfortably through the bottom of her glasses. " Take off your shoes, honey. Remember when I told you about our global crisis? How the United World Leaders Alliance banned plastic and fossil fuels and how the atmosphere stabilized." " How old were you?" Brennan asked, fascinated. " I was three when the UWLA was founded," Emily replied, scrolling as she read the article. " There was a lot of people who thought that global warming was unfounded, but-" " HA!" Grandpa staggered into the room, holding his own tablet. " You see the news? We used to live on Mars?" " Yes, Father," said Emily, looking resigned. " I know you don't believe that climate change was an issue-" " This proves it wasn't!" Grandpa shouted with all the self-important flamboyance of vindication. " See? Those Cassandran dumbasses were wrong-there WAS a Planet B!"

instruction: You are in the audience at a convicted murderer's execution, when he/she is asked for any last words, he/she scans the crowd finishing with you and looking into your eyes simply says, " I forgive you. "
reference: This was it, my only chance, humanity ’ s only chance. I had, roughly, just 30 minutes to find the mark and figure out a way to neutralize it. That was all that we could manage to calculate, even that was a guess. I am scanning the crowd furiously for the beginning, agent zero, the end of mankind as we know it. If I didn ’ t find the source of the virus it would mutate and in only 12 more years it would wipe out 76% of the population. We had no other solution, travel back and sacrifice one life to save the lives of many. The only catch was that even though we developed time travel it wasn ’ t corporeal time travel, only the consciousness could go back. While it allowed for the ability to move more freely it also prevented any physical contact with the past. The change would have to be made some other way. As I scan the crowd again it hits me, I ’ ve seen this face before, 9 years ago. An assignment from my psych class. I wrote a paper on the mind of a death row inmate. I had attended an execution to get a feel for what happens at the end of a stay on death row. As I watched them begin the injection on the inmate he looked across the crowd and stopped on me. He gazed deep into my eyes, I could almost feel him reach into me. He then said the last 3 words of his life, “ I forgive you. ” That moment stuck with me all my life but I never knew what it meant until now. I still remember it like it was yesterday but for him it is 3 years away. It was then that I knew what to do. As I entered the police officer ’ s body, my consciousness merging with his, he can see me. He can see the future that is to come. He sees what lies ahead for us. He knows there is only one answer. He unholsters his sidearm. He points the pistol at his son. He saves the world.

instruction: As chairmen of Vault-Tec, you have final say in what vault gets what purpose. While going over ideas, you come across the most absurd and ridiculous experiment idea you have ever seen. You okay it immediately and hammer out the details
reference: The physical review of the legal notes for the construction of these damn vaults is enough to make me wish for an early war. I'm sorting through the final pages of Vault 112 when I find a scuffed up post it note applied to one of the pages.'By taking away the dog's ability of clear and concise speech and giving the human subjects the dogs ability to speak we will observe the consequences of placing the humans in charge.' Damn. I read it again. Was it real? It was only on a post it note and not on official Vault-Tec stationary. What damn-fool idea that is. Nevertheless I turn to my old computer monitor and fumble through figuring out what my password was again for what felt like minutes. Once access is granted I find the file on the computer. Sure enough it is real. How can it be? If humans really cant speak than how was this contract drawn up and agreed upon. Further more I have never heard a dog speak in my life. For no good reason I approve the idea for final inclusion into Vault 112. That should entertain me for a while.

instruction: She didn't know it, but today she saved a life.
reference: WARNING: Slightly NSFW. She didn't know it, but today she saved a life. Mine, actually. I've not been having the best time of it lately- I'm late on the rent, the car just stopped working, my boss has been riding my ass and frankly... I've been struggling to think of reasons to live. I can't even remember the last time I didn't wake up trying to think of one. I was at the bar trying to brace myself. Figured, hey, why not have one last drink before I take a dive out of my window. Twelve floors head first ought to do it, but no-one wants to do that sober. Then she sat next to me. A smoking hot brunette, with skin like silk and lips like fire. She was dressed to kill in that tight little dress, and her curls framed that heart shaped face like they'd been drawn on my an artist. She was perfect. She didn't say a word to me, just grabbed my shirt and pulled me in. She never asked to kiss me, just took what she wanted. I pulled away, gasping for air. I tried to ask her her name, but she just pressed a finger to my lips and laughed. She grabbed my tie, and using it as a lead dragged me away from the bar to the disabled bathroom. I was mesmerised... entranced. It was like I couldn't say no. I fucked her hard against the bathroom door, my hands starving for her curves, wandering desperately. And then, once the fireworks had ended, she pulled up her thong, adjusted her dress and hair and winked at me. " Another time, tiger." she purred, as she left me there, confused on the floor. Suddenly, I had a reason to live, to be her. I have to know her name. I need to find her again... that dominating beauty, that vixen... The fall can wait. First I have to know her name.

instruction: " Warning: Users may be disassembled without prior notification. "
reference: *Users may be disassembled without notice. * A single statement among thousands. Nestled like a snake in the grass. *Thud~* *Thud~* *Thud~* * “ Get ready to breach! ” * Merely skimmed over by the one-in-a-million user that actually bothered to look. You ’ d think people would be more observant when their own bodies were on the line. * “ Breaching in 3…2…1… ” * Ever since Elton Co. started selling their cybernetic implants people have been willfully forfeiting their own right to live. *Bang~~* My precious antique door! Blown to smithereens by these *fools*. I rest my fingers on the button hidden under my ornate, mahogany desk, now the last memento of my trip to South America. “ Freeze! Hands where we can see them, Mr. Elton! ” I can ’ t help but grin at their overconfidence. Who do they think they are to be giving *me* orders? I flick my finger to activate the destruction sequence and recline into my elephant-leather chair. “ GAAAAH! W-What… ” “ AAAARGH! My head! ” “ The PAAAAIN! Make it stop! ” The five black-clad intruders simultaneously drop their weapons and clutch their heads in agony. Blood starts oozing from their eyes and mouths before they fall with a dull thud onto my genuine Isfahan rug. Tsk, I ’ ll have to get someone to clean that up… “ Davis! Get in here and clean up this mess. ” “ Certainly, sir. ” I look back at the bodies and notice the white letters printed on their shoulders. Hmm, CIA agents. You ’ d think *they* would be more thoughtful about these things. Seriously, does *no one* read the terms of service?

instruction: A new anti-graffiti method is put into spray paint. It now screams when it is sprayed.
reference: It was that time of year, and it seemed I was more excited than my son was. During the Cub Scout meeting that week each boy received his package for the Pinewood Derby. I remembered racing when I was a kid. Everyone would carve, paint, and decorate the small wooden block inside the package. When derby day came, we see who made the fastest race car. This would be my boy Stevie ’ s first derby. “ But, Dad... ” Stevie griped on the ride home. “ Do we have to? ” I was shocked. “ What do you mean? Making the race car is half the fun! I already went out and bought some spray paint—Red and yellow. We could call it the Flash! ” That ’ s his favorite superhero. How could he disagree with my logic? “ Todd and Davie said painting it is the worse part! ” What were those older Boy Scouts talking about? Maybe it was the paint fumes they didn ’ t like. I chalked it up to childish silliness and continued on. That weekend my daughter ’ s art supplies were moved aside to work on the car. Stevie was hesitant at first, but as we started to carve his fears went away and he was back to that little blonde fireball I know and love. “ Alright, ” I said once the time had come. I put the work-in-progress down on some old newspapers. “ We ’ ll do a base coat of primer, then make a Flash design as it dries. ” “ Do we have to paint it? ” Stevie warbled. “ Yes, yes we do. ” Great, I thought. Was this going to be a repeat of the car ride conversation again? “ Just because some of the cool, older boys don ’ t like something, doesn ’ t mean you can ’ t like it. ” I gave the spray can a shake, put my thumb on the cap, and aimed at the little chunk of wood sitting on Tuesday ’ s sports page. As soon as my finger went down, a bone cracking scream reverberated around the garage. I stopped almost instantly. “ What was that? ” I asked panicked. Looking at Stevie I saw he had his fingers in his ears. “ I told you, ” She shouted, not taking his fingers away, “ Tood and Davie say it ’ s stupid! And loud! ” I look at the spray can more closely than when I ’ d been picking the colors.'Now with anti-graffiti deterrent!' It read in bold letters at the bottom. I tried it again, and the same scream came out. There was no way we ’ d be able to paint the whole thing with a sound like that! My ears were already hurting. “ Stevie, ” I said once he ’ d unplugged his ears, “ Go ask your sister if we can borrow her puff paint. ”

instruction: This year you went all out on your Demon Halloween costume. While bar hopping downtown another guy in a very realistic demon costume invites you to a private demon themed party, you soon come to realize they are not costumes.
reference: *WOW. And here I was thinking that MY costume was impressive! These guys went ALL OUT! * I thought to myself as I wove through the crowd of scales and wings. Red, black, blue, eyestalks, horns, tails... every different body type imaginable was packed together like sardines in a can. *This is FANTASTIC! * I grinned from ear to ear as I walked toward the refreshment table. *I thought only* I *was this into demons! They got everything right! * I admired a low slung-costume that looked like a human-faced slug supported by thousands of spindly legs. *Man, how do they even MOVE that one? * I tightened the ties that held my wings and tail to my body, making sure that they were not trampled on. I wore short horns in my hair - better to not get caught on something - and had a face full of awesome facepaint and prosthetic scales that almost looked like the real thing. *HA! My costume is wayyyy better than some of these chumps. * I thought. *Heck, that guy looks like he is just wearing red facepaint and little plastic devil horns! * Finally, after spending so long feeling like a freak, I could let out my inner monster this Halloween with people just like me! " Hey babe." I winked at a woman wearing what looked to be nothing more than luminous orange body paint and a set of rams horns. She smiled back, revealing dozens of pointed fangs in the same hue as her body. *MAN! There are even hot chicks here! * I grabbed a gummy that someone had cleverly shaped to look like a rat's heart and popped it into my mouth. Instantly I spat it out again, blood dribbling down my chin. " Holy shit, these are real!?" I stammered. Suddenly, I noticed that the party had gone very quiet. The music, that had once been playing my favorite heavy metal band, was completely shut off. And every eye - even the ones that looked like they were suspended a few feet away from their owner's skulls - was on me. " Um. Hi." I said. *You know what? That mask looks awfully realistic. * " I will just be... going now." " Going?" Said a man wearing a simple tuxedo - the very man who had guided me to this party earlier tonight. " Why would we want you to do that?" He laughed, throwing his head back with false mirth. " After all... you are the main course." *** *Like it? Read more on /r/TimeSyncs! *

instruction: " I'm going to live forever or die trying. "
reference: " I'm going to live forever or die trying" " It's often an excuse used by most people to persevere and achieve the unachievable, beat the unbeatable or do the impossible. instruction: You're the most 'bitter ' in your circle, they said because you constantly mock and make fun of your lovelorn friends and their (beautiful) love lives. You think you're not.
reference: God damn Sarah is updating her Instagram again with dozens of pictures of the flowers Jack gave her to congratulate her graduating law school. Jack, the star pediatrician in the district who could heal children with just a smile. What Jack doesn't know because he was never her friend in high school was that Sarah puked into the punch bowl in prom. Not exactly a romantic image, huh, Jack? Then there's Mister I'm-Perfect-and-My-Life-Is-Perfect Christopher who just loves to rub it in people's faces that he's the happiest married man on the planet. Chris has a jaw and body that could only be matched by his husband Nathan. They got matching tattoos for reaching the summit of Kilimanjaro together and adopted 2.5 kids and half a dog. My only comfort is that Nathan has a crooked nose and limp. From serving in Afghanistan. And Rachel, oh Rachel. I thought she was going to be in the always solo train with me for the whole ride, but no, she got off a stop called " Norwegian Reggae Club". I know the world has nearly seven billion people, but there could only be a handful who even know of the genre, let alone be enthusiastic enough to start a club in some artsy-fartsy cafe that serves cruelty free coffee and gives away free meals for the homeless in which Rachel could find love. I'm not bitter. No really, I'm not. I'm not! A lot of people think that I scowl and mock my positively diabetes-inducing friends because I've never felt love and wouldn't understand it. They don't know my story, and I don't mean that in the edgy Marilyn Manson-quoting, self-help-book-consuming way. I knew someone. They laughed at everything like every exhalation would be their last; they laughed so deeply in such a way that it caught my soul and made it lighter. They held me as if I were an idol, every touch leaving prayer and longing on my starved skin. They smiled at me and all I would think of is how the sun left glitter on water as it set, the reflection calling cards that said, " Look at me, notice me before I go away!" Afternoon naps. Whispered poems. Stargazing, hushed dreams shared between each other as if just articulating them would make them come true. Indulgent midnight cakes. Dancing, spinning so that the world was just a blur, just them and I. The future. The past. " Promise me..." I-love-you's said and unsaid. I know my friends, and I know what love is like. But one day, the roses will wilt and the music will stop, and they'll wonder if they'll ever live like that ever again, without the disgust, fear, and mistakes of everyday life. They'll wonder, and nobody will be there to answer them.

instruction: " How much of a hero are you, if all you've managed to save is yourself? "
reference: He didn't mean it. But now as I sat looking down on the park from the top of a block of flats I couldn't think of anything else. He was as upset as I was that she had passed, he had just snapped and said what he wanted to say. But he didn't mean it. That wasn't making things easier. I had tried so hard. Even as I fought off depression I tried to help her out, give her the love she deserved. She couldn't read my mind like everyone else, she needed a place of solitude. Somewhere she could go without getting upset by people's thoughts. Now she was dead. And it was my fault. My heart twisted in my chest. It still hurt even now. I loved her like a sister, oh if only I had left her and let them, no then... Argh... I felt the anger building up inside me again. All the frustration and pain, focusing in on one singular point. Everyone kept telling me I should feel lucky. WHY? I'm a Monster that has been given form. A criminal locked up in a cage then handed a gun. With my head in my hands I didn't hear the chant start, only as it was getting louder and the crowd started to move out from the park did I hear. It was a pathetic chant'MUTANTS MUTANTS MUTANTS'. Was that the best they could muster? I stood up. " How much of a hero are you, if all you've managed to save is yourself?" I guess I know the answer. I took a step forward and fell straight down crashing into the pavement where people screamed as I landed. They didn't scream as I turned into a cloud of smoke, only as I started to take form and rise above them. Then they panicked. Then they ran. I lifted up my hand and dozens of protestors were thrown away, as if I was brushing dust off a table. The answer is simple. I'm not the hero. I'm the villian -- - (Kinda cheated and used the prompt to tie in with the story I'm writing:))

instruction: Colorless Green Ideas Sleep Furiously.
reference: *Kaleidoscope*, she says, and runs in colourful circles for a year. A bright, white field opens out before her, so she splashes it with orange and olive and aubergene, then runs the gamut of blues, blues, blues. And red. Such deep red, at the end. What does her creation look like, when she holds it aloft, finally, and stares into the swoops and swirls for meaning? Frantic, searching? Determined, knowing? Could anyone decrypt the long, long spirals of warm grey and cold, metal pink? Can she? Quietly, she folds it away, tucks it between the pages of a book on a shelf in a room that she never enters again, and begins to live in a structured square of more tempered hues. Well. She lives well. But still, from time to time, a turquoise look will gleam under her skin, and her thoughts turn to her bright white field where, transient and colourless, green ideas sleep furiously.

instruction: A serum is invented that brings you closer to God when injected
reference: It was my turn. Finally, I could imagine myself in a spiritual connection with the Creator. I sat in a small abandoned church, on the south side of the town we had created. It was tall, honoring our God so very well. I remember that my father must have built it, before he had been sacrificed to our true Father. I had a very simple white dress on, and I patted it down onto my pale legs. It was not like ones that I had seen on other Daughters in the villages around our town. I was excited, but thankfully not excited enough to break the ritual. And so I sat, alone, at the front pew. And there I sat, and waited for the Father. He quickly came, and off we went, down the hallway into the back of the church. He led me slowly, carrying his candle. A candle, instead of a torch or a lantern. Had he changed the Ritual? I knew I was being watched, although I knew not from where or who would be observing. The ritual did not allow for the participant to know who would see them before their meeting with the Creator of All Good. Father laid me on the bed, locking each of my arms and legs into the loose metal holds, made just for me. They were created for each Daughter for her visit, and each Son. Three months went by before each visit, each one happening on the first day of a new season. Father never told me how long the visit would be, and I only realized it now that I looked upon him. He wore his standard black clothing, the same that he preached in. But there was a name for it, and I wasn't sure what that was. " A shame, my Daughter." The Father said as I closed my eyes. He had broken the ritual, but I was too afraid of being shamed to respond. He readied the syringe and placed his hand on my arm, gripping it as he injected the serum into me. The sound of it running through my veins was the second to last thing I heard. " A true shame." **** I haven't written anything in a while, please, constructive criticism is welcome. Or just tell me if you think it's bad. Thanks!

instruction: A new engineering intern at Tegra Corp, you find yourself stumbling blindly through the hallways after a massive power failure. When the emergency lights glow, you are in a room with a massive vault. The door starts to grind open.
reference: A dull rumble vibrated the floor beneath my feet, and I could feel something happening. *Finally*. The lights had been out for almost an hour, and I had been in one of the most remote segments of the facility dropping off a package for Dr. Horz, one of the biotech R & D gurus. I had been stumbling around for what felt like ages, but my watch did confirm that it was only 56 minutes. *56 minutes of noiseless terror*. This particular R & D facility of Tegra was filled with wonders, but it was very nearly empty. I was in my second week of interning, a lowly, aspiring electrical engineer. Thus far, I had done little more than grunt work with the odd bit of logic design. Mostly just documentation though. Endless documentation. The ground stopped trembling, and the lights slowly inked a light incandescence. The walls in front of me slowly illuminated, and I was peering at a tremendous vault. A vault door—to be specific. A vault door…which was slightly cracked open. The metallic alloy comprising its structure wasn ’ t flush with the surrounding wall. And then the door started cracking open more. The noise was probably the most frightening thing. The grinding of gears and servos, attempting to hold the door shut, was echoing riotously throughout the small room. I started backing away slowly. I don ’ t know where I am. I don ’ t know what is behind that door, and I don ’ t want to be here anymore. I take a large, decisive step towards the door, and I hear a different kind of rumble—a throaty rumble, from some *thing*. And then the door quite literally gave up its effort to hold whatever was within and sprang backwards, slamming into the wall. The darkness was wholly shrouding the space beyond. A deep, primal terror was creeping into every nook of my being. What the *fuck* is happening? And then I see it. Six or seven feet in the air, slowly apparating into existence as the gentle illumination of the emergency lighting found it. A long, tube, slowly tapering to a point. No, not one. Many. The *presence* became more pronounced in the room. I watched as the objects source grew more visible. Dense, matted hair. The tubes were sprouting from it. And then the eyes. Yellow—slitted—orbs. It sprang. The last thing I perceived in those final moments, as my body was wrapped handily in a clawed grip, was a pronounced and deliberate, “ Meow. ”

instruction: God shows you 3 Doors. Door One leads to eternal happiness, Door Two leads to infinite knowledge. Then there is Door Three, and God has never opened it yet.
reference: I've been sitting at these doors for a while now. Thousands if not millions of people have passed me and chosen n a door. Everyone who passes me is always so sure of there decision.
